## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Blake](https://docs.rs/struct.BlakeTwo256.html)- Two256
- Blake2-256 Hash implementation.
- [Candidate](https://docs.rs/struct.CandidateHash.html)- Hash
- Unit type wrapper around `Hash`
- [Head](https://docs.rs/struct.HeadData.html)- Data
- Parachain head data included in the chain.
- [Hrmp](https://docs.rs/struct.HrmpChannelId.html)- Channel - Id
- A type that uniquely identifies an HRMP channel. An HRMP channel is established between two
paras. In text, we use the notation `(A, B)`to specify a channel between A and B. The channels are unidirectional, meaning that`(A, B)`and`(B, A)`refer to different channels. The convention is that we use the first item tuple for the sender and the second for the recipient. Only one channel is allowed between two participants in one direction, i.e. there cannot be 2 different channels identified by`(A, B)`. A channel with the same para id in sender and recipient is invalid. That is, however, not enforced.
- [Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)
- Unique identifier of a parachain.
- [Inbound](https://docs.rs/struct.InboundDownwardMessage.html)- Downward - Message
- A wrapped version of `DownwardMessage`. The difference is that it has attached the block number when the message was sent.
- [Inbound](https://docs.rs/struct.InboundHrmpMessage.html)- Hrmp - Message
- An HRMP message seen from the perspective of a recipient.
- [Outbound](https://docs.rs/struct.OutboundHrmpMessage.html)- Hrmp - Message
- An HRMP message seen from the perspective of a sender.
- [Slot](https://docs.rs/struct.Slot.html)
- Unit type wrapper that represents a slot.
- [Validation](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationCode.html)- Code
- Parachain validation code.
- [Validation](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationCodeHash.html)- Code - Hash
- Unit type wrapper around `Hash`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [LOWEST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LOWEST_PUBLIC_ID.html)- PUBLIC_ - ID
- The ID of the first publicly registrable parachain.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [HashT](https://docs.rs/trait.HashT.html)
- Abstraction around hashing

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Account](https://docs.rs/type.AccountId.html)- Id
- Alias to the opaque account ID type for this chain, actually a `AccountId32`. This is always 32 bytes.
- [Account](https://docs.rs/type.AccountIndex.html)- Index
- The type for looking up accounts. We don’t expect more than 4 billion of them.
- [Account](https://docs.rs/type.AccountPublic.html)- Public
- Alias to the public key used for this chain, actually a `MultiSigner`. Like the signature, this also isn’t a fixed size when encoded, as different cryptos have different size public keys.
- [Authority](https://docs.rs/type.AuthorityDiscoveryId.html)- Discovery - Id
- An authority discovery authority identifier.
- [Balance](https://docs.rs/type.Balance.html)
- The balance of an account.
128-bits (or 38 significant decimal figures) will allow for 10 m currency (`10^7`) at a resolution to all for one second’s worth of an annualised 50% reward be paid to a unit holder (`10^11`unit denomination), or`10^18`total atomic units, to grow at 50%/year for 51 years (`10^9`multiplier) for an eventual total of`10^27`units (27 significant decimal figures). We round denomination to`10^12`(12 SDF), and leave the other redundancy at the upper end so that 32 bits may be multiplied with a balance in 128 bits without worrying about overflow.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.Block.html)
- Block type.
- [BlockId](https://docs.rs/type.BlockId.html)
- Block ID.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.BlockNumber.html)- Number
- The block number type used by Polkadot. 32-bits will allow for 136 years of blocks assuming 1 block per second.
- [Downward](https://docs.rs/type.DownwardMessage.html)- Message
- A message sent from the relay-chain down to a parachain.
- [Hash](https://docs.rs/type.Hash.html)
- A hash of some data used by the relay chain.
- [Header](https://docs.rs/type.Header.html)
- Header type.
- [Horizontal](https://docs.rs/type.HorizontalMessages.html)- Messages
- [Moment](https://docs.rs/type.Moment.html)
- An instant or duration in time.
- [Nonce](https://docs.rs/type.Nonce.html)
- Index of a transaction in the relay chain. 32-bit should be plenty.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/type.SessionIndex.html)- Index
- Simple index type with which we can count sessions.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/type.Signature.html)
- Alias to type for a signature for a transaction on the relay chain. This allows one of several kinds of underlying crypto to be used, so isn’t a fixed size when encoded.
- [Upward](https://docs.rs/type.UpwardMessage.html)- Message
- A message from a parachain to its Relay Chain.

# polkadot_runtime_common - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-runtime-common/^29.0.0/

## Expand description

Common runtime code for the Relay Chain, e.g. Rococo, Westend, Polkadot, Kusama …

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use impls::`- [ToAuthor](https://docs.rs/impls/struct.ToAuthor.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [assigned_](https://docs.rs/assigned_slots/index.html)- slots
- This pallet allows to assign permanent (long-lived) or temporary
(short-lived) parachain slots to paras, leveraging the existing
parachain slot lease mechanism. Temporary slots are given turns
in a fair (though best-effort) manner.
The dispatchables must be called from the configured origin
(typically `Sudo`or a governance origin). This pallet should not be used on a production relay chain, only on a test relay chain (e.g. Rococo).
- [auctions](https://docs.rs/auctions/index.html)
- Auctioning system to determine the set of Parachains in operation. This includes logic for the auctioning mechanism and for reserving balance as part of the “payment”. Unreserving the balance happens elsewhere.
- [claims](https://docs.rs/claims/index.html)
- Pallet to process claims from Ethereum addresses.
- [crowdloan](https://docs.rs/crowdloan/index.html)
- Parachain `Crowdloaning`pallet
- [elections](https://docs.rs/elections/index.html)
- Code for elections.
- [identity_](https://docs.rs/identity_migrator/index.html)- migrator
- This pallet is designed to go into a source chain and destination chain to migrate data. The design motivations are:
- [impls](https://docs.rs/impls/index.html)
- Auxiliary `struct`/`enum`s for polkadot runtime.
- [paras_](https://docs.rs/paras_registrar/index.html)- registrar
- Pallet to handle parachain registration and related fund management.
In essence this is a simple wrapper around `paras`.
- [paras_](https://docs.rs/paras_sudo_wrapper/index.html)- sudo_ - wrapper
- A simple wrapper allowing `Sudo`to call into`paras`routines.
- [purchase](https://docs.rs/purchase/index.html)
- Pallet to process purchase of DOTs.
- [slot_](https://docs.rs/slot_range/index.html)- range
- The `SlotRange`struct which succinctly handles the 36 values that represent all sub ranges between 0 and 7 inclusive.
- [slots](https://docs.rs/slots/index.html)
- Parathread and parachains leasing system. Allows para IDs to be claimed, the code and data to be initialized and parachain slots (i.e. continuous scheduling) to be leased. Also allows for parachains and parathreads to be swapped.
- [traits](https://docs.rs/traits/index.html)
- Traits used across pallets for Polkadot.
- [xcm_](https://docs.rs/xcm_sender/index.html)- sender
- XCM sender for relay chain.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_elections_weights.html)- elections_ - weights
- Implements the weight types for the elections module and a specific
runtime.
This macro should not be called directly; use
`impl_runtime_weights`
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_runtime_weights.html)- runtime_ - weights
- Implements the weight types for a runtime.
It expects the passed runtime constants to contain a `weights`module. The generated weight types were formerly part of the common runtime but are now runtime dependant.
- [prod_](https://docs.rs/macro.prod_or_fast.html)- or_ - fast
- Macro to set a value (e.g. when using the `parameter_types`macro) to either a production value or to an environment variable or testing value (in case the`fast-runtime`feature is selected) or one of two testing values depending on feature. Note that the environment variable is evaluated*at compile time*.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adjustment](https://docs.rs/struct.AdjustmentVariable.html)- Variable
- The adjustment variable of the runtime. Higher values will cause `TargetBlockFullness`to change the fees more rapidly.
- [Assignment](https://docs.rs/struct.AssignmentSessionKeyPlaceholder.html)- Session - KeyPlaceholder
- A placeholder since there is currently no provided session key handler for parachain validator keys.
- [Balance](https://docs.rs/struct.BalanceToU256.html)- ToU256
- Convert a balance to an unsigned 256-bit number, use in nomination pools.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockHashCount.html)- Hash - Count
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockLength.html)- Length
- Maximum length of block. Up to 5MB.
- [Maximum](https://docs.rs/struct.MaximumMultiplier.html)- Multiplier
- The maximum amount of the multiplier.
- [Minimum](https://docs.rs/struct.MinimumMultiplier.html)- Multiplier
- Minimum amount of the multiplier. This value cannot be too low. A test case should ensure
that combined with `AdjustmentVariable`, we can recover from the minimum. See`multiplier_can_grow_from_zero`.
- [Parachain](https://docs.rs/struct.ParachainSessionKeyPlaceholder.html)- Session - KeyPlaceholder
- A placeholder since there is currently no provided session key handler for parachain validator keys.
- [Staking](https://docs.rs/struct.StakingBenchmarkingConfig.html)- Benchmarking - Config
- A reasonable benchmarking config for staking pallet.
- [Target](https://docs.rs/struct.TargetBlockFullness.html)- Block - Fullness
- The portion of the `NORMAL_DISPATCH_RATIO`that we adjust the fees with. Blocks filled less than this will decrease the weight and more will increase.
- [U256](https://docs.rs/struct.U256ToBalance.html)- ToBalance
- Convert an unsigned 256-bit number to balance, use in nomination pools.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Balances](https://docs.rs/enum.BalancesCall.html)- Call
- Contains a variant per dispatchable extrinsic that this pallet has.
- [Staker](https://docs.rs/enum.StakerStatus.html)- Status
- Representation of the status of a staker.
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/enum.TimestampCall.html)- Call
- Contains a variant per dispatchable extrinsic that this pallet has.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [AVERAGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.AVERAGE_ON_INITIALIZE_RATIO.html)- ON_ - INITIALIZE_ - RATIO
- We assume that an on-initialize consumes 1% of the weight on average, hence a single extrinsic
will not be allowed to consume more than `AvailableBlockRatio - 1%`.
- [MAXIMUM_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAXIMUM_BLOCK_WEIGHT.html)- BLOCK_ - WEIGHT
- We allow for 2 seconds of compute with a 6 second average block time. The storage proof size is not limited so far.
- [NORMAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.NORMAL_DISPATCH_RATIO.html)- DISPATCH_ - RATIO
- We allow `Normal`extrinsics to fill up the block up to 75%, the rest can be used by Operational extrinsics.

- Numbers which have upper and lower bounds
- [Build](https://docs.rs/trait.BuildStorage.html)- Storage
- Complex storage builder stuff.

- The type used for currency conversion.
- [Slow](https://docs.rs/type.SlowAdjustingFeeUpdate.html)- Adjusting - FeeUpdate
- Parameterized slow adjusting fee updated based on
[https://research.web3.foundation/Polkadot/overview/token-economics#2-slow-adjusting-mechanism](https://research.web3.foundation/Polkadot/overview/token-economics#2-slow-adjusting-mechanism)

# smallvec 1.15.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/smallvec/^1.11.0/

docs.rs failed to build smallvec-1.15.2

Please check the

See

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/smallvec/1.15.2/builds)for more information.See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).# rust-smallvec

"Small vector" optimization for Rust: store up to a small number of items on the stack

## Example

```
use ;

// This SmallVec can hold up to 4 items on the stack:
let mut v:  = smallvec!;
// It will automatically move its contents to the heap if
// contains more than four items:
v.push;
// SmallVec points to a slice, so you can use normal slice
// indexing and other methods to access its contents:
v = v + v;
v.sort;
```

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Get](https://docs.rs/trait.Get.html)
- A trait for querying a single value from a type.
- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/trait.Hasher.html)
- Trait describing an object that can hash a slice of bytes. Used to abstract
other types over the hashing algorithm. Defines a single `hash`method and an`Out`associated type with the necessary bounds.
- [TryCollect](https://docs.rs/trait.TryCollect.html)
- Try and collect into a collection `C`.
- [TypeId](https://docs.rs/trait.TypeId.html)
- Provide a simple 4 byte identifier for a type.
- [Typed](https://docs.rs/trait.TypedGet.html)- Get
- A trait for querying a single value from a type defined in the trait.

# sp_runtime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/^48.0.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#substrate-runtime-primitives)Substrate Runtime Primitives.

This crate, among other things, contains a large library of types and utilities that are used in
the Substrate runtime, but are not particularly `FRAME`-oriented.

[§](https://docs.rs#block-header-and-extrinsics)Block, Header and Extrinsics

Most notable, this crate contains some of the types and trait that enable important communication between the client and the runtime. This includes:

- A set of traits to declare what any block/header/extrinsic type should provide.
- A set of types that implement these traits, whilst still providing a high degree of configurability via generics.

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-api-types)Runtime API Types

This crate also contains some types that are often used in conjuncture with Runtime APIs. Most notable:

- `ApplyExtrinsicResult`- `DispatchOutcome`
- `transaction_validity`

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use generic::`- [Digest](https://docs.rs/generic/struct.Digest.html);
- `pub use generic::`- [DigestItem](https://docs.rs/generic/enum.DigestItem.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [biguint](https://docs.rs/biguint/index.html)
- Re-export big_uint stuff. Infinite precision unsigned integer for substrate runtime.
- [bounded_](https://docs.rs/bounded_btree_map/index.html)- btree_ - map
- Re-export bounded_vec and bounded_btree_map macros only when std is enabled. Traits, types and structs to support a bounded BTreeMap.
- [bounded_](https://docs.rs/bounded_vec/index.html)- vec
- Re-export bounded_vec and bounded_btree_map macros only when std is enabled. Traits, types and structs to support putting a bounded vector into storage, as a raw value, map or a double map.
- [curve](https://docs.rs/curve/index.html)
- Provides some utilities to define a piecewise linear function.
- [generic](https://docs.rs/generic/index.html)
- Generic implementations of `crate::traits::Header``crate::traits::Block``crate::traits::ExtrinsicLike`
- [helpers_](https://docs.rs/helpers_128bit/index.html)- 128bit
- Re-export 128 bit helpers. Some helper functions to work with 128bit numbers. Note that the functionality provided here is only sensible to use with 128bit numbers because for smaller sizes, you can always rely on assumptions of a bigger type (u128) being available, or simply create a per-thing and use the multiplication implementation provided there.
- [key_](https://docs.rs/key_types/index.html)- types
- Re-export this since it’s part of the API of this crate. Known key types; this also functions as a global registry of key types for projects wishing to avoid collisions with each other.
- [legacy](https://docs.rs/legacy/index.html)
- Runtime types that existed in old API versions.
- [offchain](https://docs.rs/offchain/index.html)
- A collection of higher lever helpers for offchain calls.
- [proving_](https://docs.rs/proving_trie/index.html)- trie
- Types for merkle tries compatible with the runtime.
- [runtime_](https://docs.rs/runtime_logger/index.html)- logger
- A logger that can be used to log from the runtime.
- [testing](https://docs.rs/testing/index.html)
- Testing utilities.
- [traits](https://docs.rs/traits/index.html)
- Primitives for the runtime modules.
- [transaction_](https://docs.rs/transaction_validity/index.html)- validity
- Transaction validity interface.
- [type_](https://docs.rs/type_with_default/index.html)- with_ - default
- Provides a type that wraps another type and provides a default value.

- Alias a location if it passes `Filter`and the original origin is root of`Origin`.

- Conversion implementation which converts from a `[u8; 32]`-based`AccountId`into a`Location`consisting solely of a`AccountId32`junction with a fixed value for its network (provided by`Network`) and the`AccountId`’s`[u8; 32]`datum for the`id`.

- Implementation of `Get<Vec<AssetFilter>>`which accepts every asset. (For example, it can be used with`LocationWithAssetFilters`).
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowExplicitUnpaidExecutionFrom.html)- Explicit - Unpaid - Execution - From
- Allows execution from any origin that is contained in `T`(i.e.`T::Contains(origin)`) if the message explicitly includes the`UnpaidExecution`instruction.
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowHrmpNotificationsFromRelayChain.html)- Hrmp - Notifications - From - Relay - Chain
- Allows execution for the Relay Chain origin (represented as `Location::parent()`) if it is just a straight`HrmpNewChannelOpenRequest`,`HrmpChannelAccepted`, or`HrmpChannelClosing`instruction.
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowKnownQueryResponses.html)- Known - Query - Responses
- Allows only messages if the generic `ResponseHandler`expects them via`expecting_response`.
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowSubscriptionsFrom.html)- Subscriptions - From
- Allows execution from `origin`if it is just a straight`SubscribeVersion`or`UnsubscribeVersion`instruction.
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowTopLevelPaidExecutionFrom.html)- TopLevel - Paid - Execution - From
- Allows execution from `origin`if it is contained in`T`(i.e.`T::Contains(origin)`) taking payments into account.
- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowUnpaidExecutionFrom.html)- Unpaid - Execution - From
- Allows execution from any origin that is contained in `T`(i.e.`T::Contains(origin)`).
- [AsPrefixed](https://docs.rs/struct.AsPrefixedGeneralIndex.html)- General - Index
- Converter struct implementing `AssetIdConversion`converting a numeric asset ID (must be`TryFrom/TryInto<u128>`) into a`GeneralIndex`junction, prefixed by some`Location`value. The`Location`value will typically be a`PalletInstance`junction.
- [Backing](https://docs.rs/struct.BackingToPlurality.html)- ToPlurality
- `Convert`implementation to convert from some an origin which implements- `Backing`into a corresponding- `Plurality`- `Location`.
- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeBlobDispatcher.html)- Blob - Dispatcher
- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeMessage.html)- Message
- [Case](https://docs.rs/struct.Case.html)
- Accepts an asset if it is contained in the given `T`’s`Get`implementation.
- [Child](https://docs.rs/struct.ChildParachainAsNative.html)- Parachain - AsNative
- [Child](https://docs.rs/struct.ChildParachainConvertsVia.html)- Parachain - Converts - Via
- [Child](https://docs.rs/struct.ChildSystemParachainAsSuperuser.html)- System - Parachain - AsSuperuser
- [Converted](https://docs.rs/struct.ConvertedConcreteId.html)- Concrete - Id
- [Currency](https://docs.rs/struct.CurrencyAdapter.html)- Adapter - Deprecated
- Simple adapter to use a currency as asset transactor. This type can be used as `type AssetTransactor`in`xcm::Config`.
- [Deny](https://docs.rs/struct.DenyRecursively.html)- Recursively
- Denies execution if the XCM contains instructions not meant to run on this chain,
first checking at the top-level and then **recursively**.
- [Deny](https://docs.rs/struct.DenyReserveTransferToRelayChain.html)- Reserve - Transfer - ToRelay - Chain
- [Deny](https://docs.rs/struct.DenyThenTry.html)- Then - Try
- Deny executing the XCM if it matches any of the Deny filter regardless of anything else. If it passes the Deny, and matches one of the Allow cases then it is let through.
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeAccountId32Terminal.html)- Account - Id32 - Terminal
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeAccountKey20Terminal.html)- Account - Key20 - Terminal
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeBodyTerminal.html)- Body - Terminal
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeFamily.html)- Family
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribePalletTerminal.html)- Pallet - Terminal
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeTerminus.html)- Terminus
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/struct.DescribeTreasuryVoiceTerminal.html)- Treasury - Voice - Terminal
- Create a description of the remote treasury `location`if possible. No two locations should have the same descriptor.
- [Dual](https://docs.rs/struct.DualMint.html)- Mint
- Implementation of `AssetChecking`which subjects a given set of assets`L`to having their teleportations recorded with a`MintLocation::Local`and a second set of assets`R`to having their teleportations recorded with a`MintLocation::NonLocal`.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureDecodableXcm.html)- Decodable - Xcm
- A wrapper router that attempts to *encode*and*decode*passed XCM`message`to ensure that the receiving side will be able to decode, at least with the same XCM version.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureXcmOrigin.html)- XcmOrigin
- `EnsureOrigin`barrier to convert from dispatch origin to XCM origin, if one exists.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalConsensusLocationsConverterFor.html)- Consensus - Locations - Converter - For
- Converts locations from external global consensus systems (e.g., Ethereum, other parachains)
into `AccountId`.
- [Fixed](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedLocation.html)- Location
- Adapter `struct`which implements a conversion from any`AssetKind`into a`LocatableAssetId``Location`for the`location`field.
- [Fixed](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedRateOfFungible.html)- Rate - OfFungible
- Simple fee calculator that requires payment in a single fungible at a fixed rate.
- [Fixed](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedWeightBounds.html)- Weight - Bounds
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameTransactionalProcessor.html)- Transactional - Processor
- Transactional processor implementation using frame transactional layers.
- [Fungible](https://docs.rs/struct.FungibleAdapter.html)- Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `fungible`
- [Fungible](https://docs.rs/struct.FungibleMutateAdapter.html)- Mutate - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `fungible`
- [Fungible](https://docs.rs/struct.FungibleTransferAdapter.html)- Transfer - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `fungible`
- [Fungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.FungiblesAdapter.html)- Adapter
- [Fungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.FungiblesMutateAdapter.html)- Mutate - Adapter
- [Fungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.FungiblesTransferAdapter.html)- Transfer - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`implementation to convert a- `fungibles`implementation to become usable in XCM.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalConsensusConvertsFor.html)- Consensus - Converts - For
- Converts a location which is a top-level relay chain (which provides its own consensus) into a
32-byte `AccountId`.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalConsensusParachainConvertsFor.html)- Consensus - Parachain - Converts - For
- Converts a location which is a top-level parachain (i.e. a parachain held on a
Relay-chain which provides its own consensus) into a 32-byte `AccountId`.
- [Hashed](https://docs.rs/struct.HashedDescription.html)- Description
- [Haul](https://docs.rs/struct.HaulBlobExporter.html)- Blob - Exporter
- [IsChild](https://docs.rs/struct.IsChildSystemParachain.html)- System - Parachain
- Allows a message only if it is from a system-level child parachain.
- [IsConcrete](https://docs.rs/struct.IsConcrete.html)
- Converts a `Asset`into balance`B`if its id is equal to that given by`T`’s`Get`.
- [IsParents](https://docs.rs/struct.IsParentsOnly.html)- Only
- Matches if the given location contains only the specified amount of parents and no interior junctions.
- [IsSibling](https://docs.rs/struct.IsSiblingSystemParachain.html)- System - Parachain
- Matches if the given location is a system-level sibling parachain.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalExporter.html)- Exporter
- Implementation of `SendXcm`which uses the given`ExportXcm`implementation in order to forward the message over a bridge.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalMint.html)- Mint
- Implementation of `AssetChecking`which subjects a given set of assets`T`to having their teleportations recorded with a`MintLocation::Local`.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTreasuryVoiceConvertsVia.html)- Treasury - Voice - Converts - Via
- Returns specified `TreasuryAccount`as`AccountId32`if passed`location`matches Treasury plurality.
- [Locatable](https://docs.rs/struct.LocatableAssetId.html)- Asset - Id
- Simple struct which contains both an XCM `location`and`asset_id`to identify an asset which exists on some chain.
- [Location](https://docs.rs/struct.LocationAsSuperuser.html)- AsSuperuser
- Converter that allows specific `Location`s to act as a superuser (`RuntimeOrigin::root()`) if it matches the predefined`WhitelistedSuperuserLocations`filter and`OriginKind::Superuser`.
- [Location](https://docs.rs/struct.LocationWithAssetFilters.html)- With - Asset - Filters
- Accepts a tuple `(location, assets)`if the`location`is contained in the`Contains`implementation of the given`Location`and if every asset from`assets`matches at least one of the`AssetFilter`instances provided by the`Get`implementation of`AssetFilters`.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchClasslessInstances.html)- Classless - Instances
- An adapter that implements the unified unique instances matcher `MatchesInstance``MatchesNonFungible`
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchInClassInstances.html)- InClass - Instances
- An adapter that implements the unified unique instances matcher `MatchesInstance``MatchesNonFungibles`
- [Matched](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchedConvertedConcreteId.html)- Converted - Concrete - Id
- [Matcher](https://docs.rs/struct.Matcher.html)
- Struct created from calling `fn matcher()`on a mutable slice of`Instruction`s.
- [Native](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeAsset.html)- Asset
- Accepts an asset iff it is a native asset.
- [Network](https://docs.rs/struct.NetworkExportTable.html)- Export - Table
- An adapter for the implementation of `ExporterFor`, which attempts to find the`(bridge_location, payment)`for the requested`network`and`remote_location`in the provided`T`table containing various exporters.
- [Network](https://docs.rs/struct.NetworkExportTableItem.html)- Export - Table - Item
- Configuration item representing a single exporter in the `NetworkExportTable`.
- [NoChecking](https://docs.rs/struct.NoChecking.html)
- Implementation of `AssetChecking`which subjects no assets to having their teleportations recorded.
- [NonFungible](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungibleAdapter.html)- Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungible`
- [NonFungible](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungibleMutateAdapter.html)- Mutate - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungible`
- [NonFungible](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungibleTransferAdapter.html)- Transfer - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungible`
- [NonFungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungiblesAdapter.html)- Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungibles`
- [NonFungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungiblesMutateAdapter.html)- Mutate - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungibles`
- [NonFungibles](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFungiblesTransferAdapter.html)- Transfer - Adapter
- `TransactAsset`- `nonfungibles`
- [NonLocal](https://docs.rs/struct.NonLocalMint.html)- Mint
- Implementation of `AssetChecking`which subjects a given set of assets`T`to having their teleportations recorded with a`MintLocation::NonLocal`.
- [Origin](https://docs.rs/struct.OriginToPluralityVoice.html)- ToPlurality - Voice
- `Convert`implementation to convert from an origin which passes the check of an- `EnsureOrigin`into a voice of a given pluralistic- `Body`.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.ParentAsSuperuser.html)- AsSuperuser
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.ParentIsPreset.html)- IsPreset
- A `Location``Parent``Junction``AccountId`.
- [PayOver](https://docs.rs/struct.PayOverXcmWithHelper.html)- XcmWith - Helper
- Simpler than `PayOverXcm``TransferOverXcmHelper`type.
- [Process](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessXcmMessage.html)- XcmMessage
- A message processor that delegates execution to an `XcmExecutor`.
- [Relay](https://docs.rs/struct.RelayChainAsNative.html)- Chain - AsNative
- [Respect](https://docs.rs/struct.RespectSuspension.html)- Suspension
- Barrier condition that allows for a `SuspensionChecker`that controls whether or not the XCM executor will be suspended from executing the given XCM.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/struct.SendXcmFeeToAccount.html)- XcmFee - ToAccount
- A `HandleFee`implementation that simply deposits the fees into a specific on-chain`ReceiverAccount`.
- [Sibling](https://docs.rs/struct.SiblingParachainAsNative.html)- Parachain - AsNative
- [Sibling](https://docs.rs/struct.SiblingParachainConvertsVia.html)- Parachain - Converts - Via
- [Sibling](https://docs.rs/struct.SiblingSystemParachainAsSuperuser.html)- System - Parachain - AsSuperuser
- [Signed](https://docs.rs/struct.SignedAccountId32AsNative.html)- Account - Id32 - AsNative
- [Signed](https://docs.rs/struct.SignedAccountKey20AsNative.html)- Account - Key20 - AsNative
- [Signed](https://docs.rs/struct.SignedToAccountId32.html)- ToAccount - Id32
- `Convert`implementation to convert from some a- `Signed`(system)- `Origin`into an- `AccountId32`.
- [Single](https://docs.rs/struct.SingleAssetExchangeAdapter.html)- Asset - Exchange - Adapter
- An adapter from `pallet_asset_conversion::SwapCredit``pallet_asset_conversion::QuotePrice``xcm_executor::traits::AssetExchange`
- [Sovereign](https://docs.rs/struct.SovereignPaidRemoteExporter.html)- Paid - Remote - Exporter
- Implementation of `SendXcm`which wraps the message inside an`ExportMessage`instruction and sends it to a destination known to be able to handle it.
- [Sovereign](https://docs.rs/struct.SovereignSignedViaLocation.html)- Signed - ViaLocation
- Sovereign accounts use the system’s `Signed`origin with an account ID derived from the`LocationConverter`.
- [Starts](https://docs.rs/struct.StartsWith.html)- With
- An implementation of `Contains`that checks for`Location`or`InteriorLocation`if starts with the provided type`T`.
- [Starts](https://docs.rs/struct.StartsWithExplicitGlobalConsensus.html)- With - Explicit - Global - Consensus
- An implementation of `Contains`that checks for`Location`or`InteriorLocation`if starts with expected`GlobalConsensus(NetworkId)`provided as type`T`.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.TakeWeightCredit.html)- Weight - Credit
- Execution barrier that just takes `max_weight`from`properties.weight_credit`.
- [Teleport](https://docs.rs/struct.TeleportForwarderForAccountId32.html)- Forwarder - ForAccount - Id32
- XCM adapter that implements `pallet_accumulate_and_forward::Forwarder`
- [Trailing](https://docs.rs/struct.TrailingSetTopicAsId.html)- SetTopic - AsId
- Sets the message ID to `t`using a`SetTopic(t)`in the last position if present.
- [Transfer](https://docs.rs/struct.TransferOverXcm.html)- Over - Xcm
- Transfers an asset to a beneficiary on a remote chain via XCM.
- [Transfer](https://docs.rs/struct.TransferOverXcmHelper.html)- Over - XcmHelper
- Helper type to make a transfer on another chain via XCM.
- [Unpaid](https://docs.rs/struct.UnpaidLocalExporter.html)- Local - Exporter - Deprecated
- Implementation of `SendXcm`which uses the given`ExportXcm`implementation in order to forward the message over a bridge.
- [Unpaid](https://docs.rs/struct.UnpaidRemoteExporter.html)- Remote - Exporter
- Implementation of `SendXcm`which wraps the message inside an`ExportMessage`instruction and sends it to a destination known to be able to handle it.
- [Using](https://docs.rs/struct.UsingComponents.html)- Components
- Weight trader which uses the configured `WeightToFee`to set the right price for weight and then places any weight bought into the right account.
- [Weight](https://docs.rs/struct.WeightInfoBounds.html)- Info - Bounds
- [With](https://docs.rs/struct.WithComputedOrigin.html)- Computed - Origin
- A derivative barrier, which scans the first `MaxPrefixes`instructions for origin-alterers and then evaluates`should_execute`of the`InnerBarrier`based on the remaining instructions and the newly computed origin.
- [With](https://docs.rs/struct.WithLatestLocationConverter.html)- Latest - Location - Converter
- An adapter implementation of `MaybeEquivalence`which can convert between the latest`Location`and other versions that implement`TryInto<Location>`and`TryFrom<Location>`.
- [With](https://docs.rs/struct.WithTopicSource.html)- Topic - Source
- Wrapper router which, if the message does not already end with a `SetTopic`instruction, prepends one to the message filled with an ID from`TopicSource`. This ID is returned from a successful`deliver`.
- [With](https://docs.rs/struct.WithUniqueTopic.html)- Unique - Topic
- Wrapper router which, if the message does not already end with a `SetTopic`instruction, appends one to the message filled with a universally unique ID. This ID is returned from a successful`deliver`.
- [XcmFee](https://docs.rs/struct.XcmFeeManagerFromComponents.html)- Manager - From - Components
- A `FeeManager`implementation that permits the specified`WaivedLocations`to not pay for fees and that uses the provided`HandleFee`implementation otherwise.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Dispatch](https://docs.rs/enum.DispatchBlobError.html)- Blob - Error
- [Haul](https://docs.rs/enum.HaulBlobError.html)- Blob - Error
- [Mint](https://docs.rs/enum.MintLocation.html)- Location
- The location which is allowed to mint a particular asset.
- [Transfer](https://docs.rs/enum.TransferStatus.html)- Status
- Status for making a payment via the `Pay::pay`trait function.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Asset](https://docs.rs/trait.AssetChecking.html)- Checking
- Simple trait to indicate whether an asset is subject to having its teleportation into and out of
this chain recorded and if so in what `MintLocation`.
- [Controller](https://docs.rs/trait.Controller.html)
- Umbrella trait for all Controller traits.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateMatcher.html)- Matcher
- Creates an instruction matcher from an XCM. Since XCM versions differ, we need to make a trait here to unify the interfaces among them.
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/trait.DescribeLocation.html)- Location
- Means of converting a location into a stable and unique descriptive identifier.
- [Dispatch](https://docs.rs/trait.DispatchBlob.html)- Blob
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/trait.EnsureDelivery.html)- Delivery
- Trait for a type which ensures all requirements for successful delivery with XCM transport layers.
- [Execute](https://docs.rs/trait.ExecuteController.html)- Controller
- Execute an XCM locally, for a given origin.
- [Execute](https://docs.rs/trait.ExecuteControllerWeightInfo.html)- Controller - Weight - Info
- Weight functions needed for `ExecuteController`
- [Exporter](https://docs.rs/trait.ExporterFor.html)- For
- [Handle](https://docs.rs/trait.HandleFee.html)- Fee
- Handles the fees that are taken by certain XCM instructions.
- [Haul](https://docs.rs/trait.HaulBlob.html)- Blob
- [Inspect](https://docs.rs/trait.InspectMessageQueues.html)- Message - Queues
- Inspects messages in queues. Meant to be used in runtime APIs, not in runtimes.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/trait.MatchXcm.html)- Xcm
- API that allows to pattern-match against anything that is contained within an XCM.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/trait.QueryController.html)- Controller
- Query a remote location, from a given origin.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/trait.QueryControllerWeightInfo.html)- Controller - Weight - Info
- Weight functions needed for `QueryController`
- [Query](https://docs.rs/trait.QueryHandler.html)- Handler
- Provides methods to expect responses from XCMs and query their status.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/trait.SendController.html)- Controller
- Send an XCM from a given origin.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/trait.SendControllerWeightInfo.html)- Controller - Weight - Info
- Weight functions needed for `SendController`
- [Take](https://docs.rs/trait.TakeRevenue.html)- Revenue
- Function trait for handling some revenue. Similar to a negative imbalance (credit) handler, but
for a `Asset`. Sensible implementations will deposit the asset in some known treasury or block-author account.
- [Transfer](https://docs.rs/trait.Transfer.html)
- Is intended to be implemented using a `fungible`impl, but can also be implemented with XCM/Asset and made generic over assets.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [deposit_](https://docs.rs/fn.deposit_or_burn_fee.html)- or_ - burn_ - fee
- Try to deposit the given fee in the specified account. Burns the fee in case of a failure.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_is_remote.html)- is_ - remote
- Returns the network ID and consensus location within that network of the remote
location `dest`which is itself specified as a location relative to the local chain, itself situated at`universal_local`within the consensus universe. If`dest`is not a location in remote consensus, then an error is returned.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Converted](https://docs.rs/type.ConvertedConcreteAssetId.html)- Concrete - Asset - Id - Deprecated
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/type.DescribeAccountIdTerminal.html)- Account - IdTerminal
- [Describe](https://docs.rs/type.DescribeAllTerminal.html)- AllTerminal
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/type.ForeignChainAliasAccount.html)- Chain - Alias - Account - Deprecated
- This is deprecated in favor of the more modular `HashedDescription`converter. If your chain has previously used this, then you can retain backwards compatibility using`HashedDescription`and a tuple with`LegacyDescribeForeignChainAccount`as the first element. For example:
- [PayAccount](https://docs.rs/type.PayAccountId32OnChainOverXcm.html)- Id32 - OnChain - Over - Xcm
- Specialization of the `PayOverXcm``[u8; 32]`-based`AccountId`values to be paid on a remote chain.
- [PayOver](https://docs.rs/type.PayOverXcm.html)- Xcm
- Implementation of the `frame_support::traits::tokens::Pay`trait, to allow for XCM-based payments of a given`Balance`of some asset ID existing on some chain under ownership of some`Interior`location of the local chain to a particular`Beneficiary`. The`AssetKind`value is not itself bounded (to avoid the issue of needing to wrap some preexisting datatype), however a converter type`AssetKindToLocatableAsset`must be provided in order to translate it into a`LocatableAsset`, which comprises both an XCM`Location`describing the XCM endpoint on which the asset to be paid resides and an XCM`AssetId`to identify the specific asset at that endpoint.

# kigumi-mod-base 1.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-mod-base/1.0.0

Base module: the foundational models other modules build on — currency, partner (contacts), and company. Root of the dependency graph (no dependencies of its own).

Multi-company: `res.company` is the unit of data isolation; transactional models carry a
`company_id` (added per model, e.g. sale.order). Partners are shared (no company_id) to avoid a
circular FK with res.company; company-specific contacts can be modelled later behind a deferred
FK. The active-company filtering rule lives in the security layer (Ctx.company + a record rule).

---

                Kigumi base module: foundational models (res.partner, res.currency)

# kigumi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Facade for the Kigumi framework. Application modules depend only on this crate.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use kigumi_core::`- [inventory](https://docs.rs/inventory/0.3.24/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/inventory/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Everything needed to define a module: `use kigumi::prelude::*;`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_acls.html)- acls
- Registers a module’s ACLs so a server collects them via `registered_acls()`. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_acls!(ACLS);`where`ACLS: &'static [Acl]`.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_action.html)- action
- Registers a state-transition action on a model, runnable via `POST /api/<model>/<id>/action/<name>`.`kigumi::register_action!("sale.order", "confirm", confirm_order, &["sales.user"]);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_compute.html)- compute
- Registers a compute function by name, so the engine runs it on write for fields declaring it.
Use at module top level: `kigumi::register_compute!("compute_total", compute_total);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_constraint.html)- constraint
- Registers a cross-record constraint (Odoo `@api.constrains`):`func`runs in the write transaction after the record + its children are written, and returns`Err(msg)`to reject (roll back) the write.`fields`are the triggers (empty = every write); list the WRITTEN fields and One2many field names that drive the invariant, plus any stored computed field it reads (those also trigger on update). Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_constraint!("account.move", &["line_ids"], check_balanced);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_external.html)- external
- Marks a model’s table as owned outside the metamodel (Odoo’s `_auto = False`): the model is resolved/served normally but migration never creates or alters its table. For models mapped onto a pre-existing table (e.g.`res.users`onto the auth subsystem’s`kigumi_user`) or a SQL view. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_external!("res.users");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_field_groups.html)- field_ - groups
- Restricts a model field to the given groups (D6 field-level security): read AND write of that
field require membership in at least one group; superuser bypasses. Usually emitted automatically
by `#[field(groups = "...")]`, but can be declared by hand:`kigumi::register_field_groups!("res.users", "login", &["admin"]);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_inherits.html)- inherits
- Declares delegation inheritance (Odoo’s `_inherits`):`model`exposes`parent`’s stored scalar fields through its required Many2one`via`FK. Usually emitted by`#[model(inherits=…, via=…)]`:`kigumi::register_inherits!("product.product", "product.template", "product_tmpl_id");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_job.html)- job
- Registers a BACKGROUND JOB kind, runnable ad hoc with retries: enqueue with
`Db::enqueue_job(name, payload)`or — transactionally, inside a service — with`ServiceCtx::enqueue_job`.`func`is an`async fn(&Db, Json) -> Result<(), DbError>`; a returned Err retries with exponential backoff up to`max_attempts`(then dead-letters). Bodies MUST be idempotent (at-least-once execution).`kigumi::register_job!("send_invoice_mail", 8, send_mail);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_ledger_report.html)- ledger_ - report
- Registers a read-only LEDGER REPORT (record-less aggregate query, returning JSON rows) runnable via
`GET /api/reports/<name>`— distinct from`register_report!`, which is the per-record document/PDF engine.`func`is an`async fn(&PgPool, params) -> Result<Vec<Json>, DbError>`;`read_model`is the model whose Read ACL gates it. The macro emits the one`Box::pin`adapting the async fn to the fn ptr.`kigumi::register_ledger_report!("trial_balance", "account.account", trial_balance, &[]);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_mailed.html)- mailed
- Opts a model into the mail subsystem (chatter): it gains a thread of messages, followers and
activities via the `(res_model, res_id)`link, and the framework cleans that thread up when the record is deleted. One line, no mixin:`kigumi::register_mailed!("sale.order");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_migration.html)- migration
- Registers a versioned DATA migration for a module — the upgrade contract. It runs when migrate
finds the module installed at a ledger version < `to_version`while the linked crate is
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_module.html)- module
- Registers a module’s manifest in the global catalog, so `resolve_modules`can see it. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_module!(MANIFEST);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_related.html)- related
- Marks a field as a `related`field (Odoo`related=`): a non-stored, read-only mirror of the value reached by`path`(e.g. “order_id.currency_id”). Usually emitted by`#[field(related = "...")]`.`kigumi::register_related!("sale.order.line", "order_currency_id", "order_id.currency_id");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_report.html)- report
- Registers a report on a model: a pure render fn producing an HTML document for one record, exposed
at `GET /api/<model>/<id>/report/<name>`(secured by read access to the record) and listed in the model’s UI contract.`name`is the URL segment,`title`the human label. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_report!("sale.order", "quotation", "Quotation", render_quotation);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_route.html)- route
- Registers a MODULE HTTP ROUTE on the generic dispatch `GET|POST /api/x/<name>`— bespoke module endpoints (an inbound-webhook receiver, a custom search) without the module ever depending on the server crate or axum.`method`is a RouteMethod variant name (Get|Post);`auth: false`runs the body under the GUEST context (uid −1, no groups — the default-deny ACL blocks every secured call, so verify the sender yourself — use`RouteInput::verify_hmac_sha256`or your provider’s exact scheme with a CONSTANT-TIME comparison, never a hand-rolled hash +`==`— then elevate via`.sudo()`. Query/body/header values are anonymous input: bind them in SQL, never interpolate).`kigumi::register_route!("stripe-hook", Post, false, &[], stripe_hook);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_rules.html)- rules
- Registers a module’s record rules so a server collects them via `registered_rules()`. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_rules!(RULES);`where`RULES: &'static [RecordRule]`.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_seed.html)- seed
- Registers a module’s idempotent reference-data seeder, run at every migrate while the module
is installed (in dependency order). Bodies must never overwrite operator changes — guard with
count/exists checks: the DB is the authority. `func`is an`async fn(&Db) -> Result<(), DbError>`.`kigumi::register_seed!("base", seed::seed_base_data);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_sequence.html)- sequence
- Registers a document-numbering sequence, declared by the module whose action consumes it
(`ActionOutcome::assign_sequence`). Ensured at migrate; an existing sequence keeps its counter.`kigumi::register_sequence!("sales", "SO", "SO/", "", 5);`→ SO/00001.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_service.html)- service
- Registers a cross-record SERVICE on a model, runnable via `POST /api/<model>/<id>/service/<name>`. The transactional twin of`register_action!`:`func`is a`async fn(&mut ServiceCtx, ServiceInput) -> Result<ServiceOutput, DbError>`that owns multi-record logic through the secured`ServiceCtx`.`write_gate`is`true`for a mutating service,`false`for a read-only one (a report). The macro emits the one`Box::pin`that adapts the async fn to the stored fn pointer.`kigumi::register_service!("sale.order.discount", "apply_discount", apply_discount, true, &["sales.user"]);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_tracked.html)- tracked
- Marks a field as tracked (Odoo’s `tracking=True`): a change to it on a mailed model records a`notification`message + a typed`mail.tracking`row in the chatter. Usually emitted by`#[field(tracked)]`, but can be declared by hand:`kigumi::register_tracked!("sale.order", "state");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_transient.html)- transient
- Marks a model as transient (Odoo’s `TransientModel`): a wizard scratchpad whose rows are ephemeral. The model is served + secured like any model, but an hourly GC cron reclaims rows by age, and migration gives its`create_date`column a`DEFAULT now()`so every insert is stamped. The model must declare a nullable`create_date: Datetime`. One line:`kigumi::register_transient!("sale.order.discount");`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_view.html)- view
- Registers a model’s form layout (Odoo’s form arch, minimal): titled groups of scalar fields plus a
notebook of tabbed pages. Emitted in the model’s UI contract so the frontend renders a real view
instead of dumping fields in declaration order. Use at module top level:
`kigumi::register_view!("product.product", &[ FieldGroup { .. } ], &[ NotebookPage { .. } ]);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_wizard.html)- wizard
- Registers a wizard: binds a transient `model`to its`default_get`(the server-side seed computed from the open context), exposing`POST /api/<model>/open`. The model must also be`register_transient!`-marked. Apply logic is a dedicated per-wizard service method + endpoint (like`apply_pricelist`), not part of this registration. Use at module top level:`kigumi::register_wizard!("sale.order.discount", default_get_discount);`
- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_write_trigger.html)- write_ - trigger
- Registers an in-tx WRITE TRIGGER: `func`runs on the caller’s transaction after a secured write to`model`when one of`watch`columns changed (empty = every write), for a stored effect the`depends`recompute can’t express on read — e.g. a Many2many aggregate summed across a join.`func`is an`async fn(&mut Transaction, id, changed_cols) -> Result<(), DbError>`; a returned`Err`rolls the write back. The macro emits the one`Box::pin`adapting the async fn to the stored fn pointer.`kigumi::register_write_trigger!("product.template.attribute.value", &["price_extra"], recompute);`

---

# serde_json - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_json/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-json)Serde JSON

JSON is a ubiquitous open-standard format that uses human-readable text to transmit data objects consisting of key-value pairs.

```
{
    "name": "John Doe",
    "age": 43,
    "address": {
        "street": "10 Downing Street",
        "city": "London"
    },
    "phones": [
        "+44 1234567",
        "+44 2345678"
    ]
}
```
There are three common ways that you might find yourself needing to work with JSON data in Rust.

- **As text data.**An unprocessed string of JSON data that you receive on an HTTP endpoint, read from a file, or prepare to send to a remote server.
- **As an untyped or loosely typed representation.**Maybe you want to check that some JSON data is valid before passing it on, but without knowing the structure of what it contains. Or you want to do very basic manipulations like insert a key in a particular spot.
- **As a strongly typed Rust data structure.**When you expect all or most of your data to conform to a particular structure and want to get real work done without JSON’s loosey-goosey nature tripping you up.

Serde JSON provides efficient, flexible, safe ways of converting data between each of these representations.

[§](https://docs.rs#operating-on-untyped-json-values)Operating on untyped JSON values

Any valid JSON data can be manipulated in the following recursive enum
representation. This data structure is [ serde_json::Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html).

```
enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(Number),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(Map<String, Value>),
}
```
A string of JSON data can be parsed into a `serde_json::Value` by the
[ serde_json::from_str](https://docs.rs/fn.from_str.html) function. There is also

[for parsing from a byte slice](https://docs.rs/fn.from_slice.html)

`from_slice``&[u8]` and [for parsing from any](https://docs.rs/fn.from_reader.html)

`from_reader``io::Read` like a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde_json::{Result, Value};
fn untyped_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into serde_json::Value.
    let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Access parts of the data by indexing with square brackets.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", v["name"], v["phones"][0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
The result of square bracket indexing like `v["name"]` is a borrow of the
data at that index, so the type is `&Value`. A JSON map can be indexed with
string keys, while a JSON array can be indexed with integer keys. If the
type of the data is not right for the type with which it is being indexed,
or if a map does not contain the key being indexed, or if the index into a
vector is out of bounds, the returned element is `Value::Null`.

When a `Value` is printed, it is printed as a JSON string. So in the code
above, the output looks like `Please call "John Doe" at the number "+44 1234567"`. The quotation marks appear because `v["name"]` is a `&Value`
containing a JSON string and its JSON representation is `"John Doe"`.
Printing as a plain string without quotation marks involves converting from
a JSON string to a Rust string with [ as_str()](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html#method.as_str) or avoiding the use of

`Value` as described in the following section.The `Value` representation is sufficient for very basic tasks but can be
tedious to work with for anything more significant. Error handling is
verbose to implement correctly, for example imagine trying to detect the
presence of unrecognized fields in the input data. The compiler is powerless
to help you when you make a mistake, for example imagine typoing `v["name"]`
as `v["nmae"]` in one of the dozens of places it is used in your code.

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-json-as-strongly-typed-data-structures)Parsing JSON as strongly typed data structures

Serde provides a powerful way of mapping JSON data into Rust data structures largely automatically.

```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn typed_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into a Person object. This is exactly the
    // same function as the one that produced serde_json::Value above, but
    // now we are asking it for a Person as output.
    let p: Person = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Do things just like with any other Rust data structure.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", p.name, p.phones[0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
This is the same `serde_json::from_str` function as before, but this time we
assign the return value to a variable of type `Person` so Serde will
automatically interpret the input data as a `Person` and produce informative
error messages if the layout does not conform to what a `Person` is expected
to look like.

Any type that implements Serde’s `Deserialize` trait can be deserialized
this way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>`
and `HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Deserialize)]`.

Once we have `p` of type `Person`, our IDE and the Rust compiler can help us
use it correctly like they do for any other Rust code. The IDE can
autocomplete field names to prevent typos, which was impossible in the
`serde_json::Value` representation. And the Rust compiler can check that
when we write `p.phones[0]`, then `p.phones` is guaranteed to be a
`Vec<String>` so indexing into it makes sense and produces a `String`.

[§](https://docs.rs#constructing-json-values)Constructing JSON values

Serde JSON provides a [ json! macro](https://docs.rs/macro.json.html) to build

`serde_json::Value`
objects with very natural JSON syntax.```
use serde_json::json;
fn main() {
    // The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
    let john = json!({
        "name": "John Doe",
        "age": 43,
        "phones": [
            "+44 1234567",
            "+44 2345678"
        ]
    });
    println!("first phone number: {}", john["phones"][0]);
    // Convert to a string of JSON and print it out
    println!("{}", john.to_string());
}
```
The `Value::to_string()` function converts a `serde_json::Value` into a
`String` of JSON text.

One neat thing about the `json!` macro is that variables and expressions can
be interpolated directly into the JSON value as you are building it. Serde
will check at compile time that the value you are interpolating is able to
be represented as JSON.

```
let full_name = "John Doe";
let age_last_year = 42;
// The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
let john = json!({
    "name": full_name,
    "age": age_last_year + 1,
    "phones": [
        format!("+44 {}", random_phone())
    ]
});
```
This is amazingly convenient, but we have the problem we had before with
`Value`: the IDE and Rust compiler cannot help us if we get it wrong. Serde
JSON provides a better way of serializing strongly-typed data structures
into JSON text.

[§](https://docs.rs#creating-json-by-serializing-data-structures)Creating JSON by serializing data structures

A data structure can be converted to a JSON string by
[ serde_json::to_string](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html). There is also

[which serializes to a](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec.html)

`serde_json::to_vec``Vec<u8>` and
[which serializes to any](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer.html)

`serde_json::to_writer``io::Write`
such as a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Address {
    street: String,
    city: String,
}
fn print_an_address() -> Result<()> {
    // Some data structure.
    let address = Address {
        street: "10 Downing Street".to_owned(),
        city: "London".to_owned(),
    };
    // Serialize it to a JSON string.
    let j = serde_json::to_string(&address)?;
    // Print, write to a file, or send to an HTTP server.
    println!("{}", j);
    Ok(())
}
```
Any type that implements Serde’s `Serialize` trait can be serialized this
way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>` and
`HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Serialize)]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

As long as there is a memory allocator, it is possible to use serde_json without the rest of the Rust standard library. Disable the default “std” feature and enable the “alloc” feature:

```
[dependencies]
serde_json = { version = "1.0", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
```
For JSON support in Serde without a memory allocator, please see the
[ serde-json-core](https://github.com/rust-embedded-community/serde-json-core) crate.

# kigumi_auth - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-auth/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Authentication: password hashing (argon2) and signed (HS256 JWT) access/refresh tokens.

Tokens are TYPED: an `access` token verifies into a [ Ctx](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Ctx.html) for data requests; a

`refresh`
token only proves identity to mint a new access token. A refresh token can NEVER be used as a
bearer for data access, and vice versa (the `kind` claim is checked) — this prevents a
long-lived refresh token from acting as a god-mode bearer. JWT crypto is delegated to the
battle-tested `jsonwebtoken` crate; passwords use argon2.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Authenticator](https://docs.rs/struct.Authenticator.html)
- Issues and verifies HS256 tokens with a shared secret.
- [Refresh](https://docs.rs/struct.RefreshClaims.html)- Claims
- The verified identity carried by a refresh token.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_password.html)- password
- Hashes a password with argon2 (random salt). Store the returned PHC string.
- [new_jti](https://docs.rs/fn.new_jti.html)
- A random 128-bit token id (hex) for refresh-token tracking.
- [verify_](https://docs.rs/fn.verify_password.html)- password
- Verifies a password against a stored argon2 hash (constant-time inside argon2).

# kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Postgres persistence layer.

Closes the loop: the metamodel’s generated DDL creates real tables, and a [ Domain](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/domain/enum.Domain.html) is
compiled to a PARAMETERIZED

`WHERE` whose values are BOUND (never interpolated) before
execution. The `*_secured` methods enforce the security engine (ACL + record rules) at the
database boundary: access is checked, and the user’s record-rule domain is AND-ed into the
query — so a user can never read rows the rules forbid.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AclRow](https://docs.rs/struct.AclRow.html)
- One configured ACL row (for listing/inspection).
- [Cron](https://docs.rs/struct.CronRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a scheduled job (emitted by hand or a future `register_cron!`).
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomField.html)- Field
- A runtime-defined field. Strings are owned (they come from the DB, not the compile-time `'static`catalog); the host leaks them when it builds a`FieldDef`.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataMigrationRegistration.html)- Migration - Registration
- [Db](https://docs.rs/struct.Db.html)
- A connection pool to a Postgres database. `Clone`shares the same pool (cheap;`PgPool`is an`Arc`internally) — e.g. to hand a handle to the background cron scheduler.
- [JobRegistration](https://docs.rs/struct.JobRegistration.html)
- Registration of a job kind, emitted by `register_job!`.`max_attempts`counts executions, not retries: 1 = never retry; the webhook-parity default in the macro is 8.
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/struct.LedgerReportRegistration.html)- Report - Registration
- Registration of a report by name, emitted by `register_report!`.`read_model`is the model whose Read ACL gates it (e.g. account.account);`groups`(if non-empty) further restricts who may run it.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListPage.html)- Page
- A page of list results plus the total count under the same secured domain.
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/struct.Migration.html)
- One migration step: the SQL that brings a module’s schema/data up to `version`.
- [Outbox](https://docs.rs/struct.OutboxEvent.html)- Event
- A domain event to enqueue. `change_summary`is small JSON metadata (changed fields, a deleted row’s last snapshot, a state transition) — never the full record, which the dispatcher reads fresh at delivery so a webhook always reflects committed truth.
- [Outgoing](https://docs.rs/struct.OutgoingMail.html)- Mail
- One queued outgoing email handed to the host’s SMTP transport by `Db::flush_outgoing_mail`
- [Route](https://docs.rs/struct.RouteInput.html)- Input
- Everything a module route body receives, expressed in DB/JSON terms (no axum types):
the caller context (authenticated, or the GUEST context for `auth: false`routes), the query params, the parsed JSON body (empty when the body is not a JSON object — NOT an error: webhook senders post forms and raw payloads), the EXACT raw bytes (HMAC signature verification must hash what was sent, not a re-serialization), and the request headers (lowercased names, duplicate values joined with “, “).
- [Route](https://docs.rs/struct.RouteRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a module HTTP route, emitted by `register_route!`. Keyed by (name, method) — a provider like Meta uses GET for its verification handshake and POST for delivery on the SAME path.`auth: true`routes require a bearer (plus the optional group gate);`auth: false`routes run under the GUEST context — uid −1, NO groups, non-su — which the default-deny ACL engine blocks from every secured read/write, so the body must authenticate the caller itself (e.g. an HMAC signature over`raw_body`) and then elevate explicitly via`Ctx::sudo`(the same greppable idiom as`ServiceCtx::elevated`).
- [RuleRow](https://docs.rs/struct.RuleRow.html)
- One configured DB record rule (for listing/inspection).
- [Seed](https://docs.rs/struct.SeedRegistration.html)- Registration
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceCtx.html)- Ctx
- The secured-primitive surface handed to a service body. A concrete struct (no trait, no `dyn`): its methods are`async fn`s delegating to`Db`’s secured CRUD under the caller’s context, so the security engine is re-applied on every call. The ERP model-name literals a body resolves live in the MODULE, never in this crate.
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceInput.html)- Input
- The route `:id`plus the POST JSON body (e.g. a payment`{amount, journal_id}`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceOutput.html)- Output
- What a service returns: free-form JSON the handler relays verbatim (services produce a result — an id,
a count, a report — not a same-record diff like an `ActionOutcome`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a service by (model, name) — the transactional twin of `ActionRegistration`.`write_gate`selects the ACL operation the dispatcher checks (Write for a mutating service, Read for a read-only one such as a report).`groups`(if non-empty) restricts who may run it, on top of the ACL.
- [Stored](https://docs.rs/struct.StoredEvent.html)- Event
- One outbox row as the live event stream reads it — the SSE counterpart of the webhook envelope.
- [UserRow](https://docs.rs/struct.UserRow.html)
- A user row used for credential verification.
- [View](https://docs.rs/struct.ViewOverride.html)- Override
- A runtime UI override for one field. `label`/`widget`replace the contract value when set;`invisible`drops the field from the served contract;`readonly`locks it;`invisible_when`/`readonly_when`carry a JSON domain AST for conditional visibility/lock. All fields are data — none reaches DDL.
- [Webhook](https://docs.rs/struct.WebhookDelivery.html)- Delivery
- A claimed delivery handed to the host’s HTTP transport. `payload["id"]`(evt_) is the stable idempotency key across retries; `attempts`is the count BEFORE this attempt.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteTriggerRegistration.html)- Trigger - Registration
- Registration of a write trigger, emitted by `register_write_trigger!`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/enum.MigrationOutcome.html)- Outcome
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteMethod.html)- Method
- HTTP method of a module route. An enum here (not an http-crate type) keeps this crate HTTP-free; the server translates. Get also serves HEAD (axum’s default).
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteOutput.html)- Output
- What a module route returns: JSON (the normal case) or PLAIN TEXT — some webhook providers’ challenge handshakes require echoing a token as an unquoted text body (a JSON string would be quoted and fail their exact-match).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_safe_ident.html)- safe_ - ident
- A Postgres identifier safe to interpolate into DDL: lowercase start, then letters/digits/underscore.
Custom-field names and the model table are validated against this before any `ALTER TABLE`.
- [job_for](https://docs.rs/fn.job_for.html)
- Looks up a registered job kind.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_for.html)- report_ - for
- Looks up a registered report by name.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_names.html)- report_ - names
- All registered report names (for a UI report menu).
- [m2m_](https://docs.rs/fn.m2m_junction_ddl.html)- junction_ - ddl
- Builds the SELECT column list for a model. NUMERIC columns are cast to float8 so they decode
into `f64`without a decimal dependency. Identifiers come from the model, never user input. Registered models that have a One2many field targeting`child_model_name`, paired with the inverse FK column — i.e. the aggregate parents to recompute when such a child changes. The exact junction-table DDL for a model’s Many2many fields — the single source shared by`Db::create_m2m_relations`
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_crons.html)- crons
- All compile-time-registered cron jobs.
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_for.html)- for
- Looks up a route by (name, method).
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_methods.html)- methods
- The methods registered under `name`(for the 405 Allow header when the method doesn’t match).
- [service_](https://docs.rs/fn.service_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered service by model + name.
- [services_](https://docs.rs/fn.services_for.html)- for
- All services registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can render its service buttons).
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_routes.html)- routes
- Startup validation of the route registry: names must be single path segments (the generic
`/api/x/:route`route can’t match a slash) and (name, method) must be unique. Call once when building the router; a violation is an authoring bug, not a runtime condition.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_triggers_for.html)- triggers_ - for
- The write triggers registered on `model`(empty when none — the common case, iterated per secured write).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BoxService](https://docs.rs/type.BoxServiceFut.html)- Fut
- A boxed Send future borrowing the `&mut ServiceCtx`for lifetime`'c`— what lets a service body`.await`secured-CRUD calls while holding the context borrow.
- [CronFn](https://docs.rs/type.CronFn.html)
- A scheduled job’s body. The returned future borrows `db`for the duration of the run.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/type.DataMigrationFn.html)- Migration - Fn
- A versioned per-module DATA migration (emitted by `register_migration!`): the upgrade contract. Runs when migrate finds the module installed at a ledger version <`to_version`while the linked crate is >=`to_version`. Steps run in semver order, each bumping the ledger to its`to_version`— a failed upgrade resumes exactly where it stopped, so bodies must be idempotent (at-least-once, like jobs). A fresh install runs no migrations: the declarative schema is already current-shape, and the ledger starts at the linked version.
- [JobFn](https://docs.rs/type.JobFn.html)
- A registered job body: owns its payload, reaches the DB through the full handle (same trust
class as a cron body). Return `Err`to schedule a retry (or dead-letter past`max_attempts`).
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/type.LedgerReportFn.html)- Report - Fn
- A read-only REPORT fn — bespoke aggregate SQL over the pool returning JSON rows, with optional query params. The read-only, record-less sibling of a service (a report has no record id): gated only on Read of a declared model, then dispatched generically. The ERP report logic lives in the module that owns the tables; the core just gates + dispatches.
- [RouteFn](https://docs.rs/type.RouteFn.html)
- A registered module route body: bespoke logic over the full `Db`handle. Same trust class as a service body (`ServiceCtx::pool`already hands services the raw pool past the gate): module code is trusted first-party code once it compiles; AUTHORIZATION is the dispatcher’s job.
- [SeedFn](https://docs.rs/type.SeedFn.html)
- A module’s reference-data seeder (emitted by `register_seed!`). Runs at EVERY migrate for installed modules, in dependency order — so bodies must be idempotent and never overwrite an operator change (guard with count/exists checks: the DB is the authority).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/type.ServiceFn.html)- Fn
- A registered service fn. A HRTB plain `fn`pointer (so it is storable in`inventory`, like`ActionFn`) returning a boxed future whose lifetime is tied to the`&mut ServiceCtx`borrow. Module authors write a bare`async fn(&mut ServiceCtx, ServiceInput) -> Result<ServiceOutput, DbError>`and`register_service!`wraps it with the one`Box::pin`.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/type.WriteTriggerFn.html)- Trigger - Fn
- An in-tx WRITE TRIGGER — a module hook that runs on the caller’s transaction AFTER a secured write to
`model`, when one of`watch`ed columns changed (empty = any). The framework’s own`depends`-driven recompute handles same-record + child aggregates; this seam covers the effects it can’t express on read — chiefly a Many2many aggregate stored across a join (e.g. a product variant’s`price_extra`summed over its attribute-value cells). Runs on`&mut Transaction`only (no ACL re-entry), so it stays a pure, engine-owned in-tx side effect, atomic with the write. ZERO ERP literals reach this crate — the model name and the SQL live in the module that owns the tables.
