}## Expand description

The general nature of an error. The purpose of this enum is not to describe the error itself, but rather to describe how the client might want to respond to the error.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Failed)

### Failed

Something went wrong

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Overloaded)

### Overloaded

The call failed because of a temporary lack of resources. This could be space resources (out of memory, out of disk space) or time resources (request queue overflow, operation timed out).

The operation might work if tried again, but it should NOT be repeated immediately as this may simply exacerbate the problem.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Disconnected)

### Disconnected

The call required communication over a connection that has been lost. The caller will need to re-establish connections and try again.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unimplemented)

### Unimplemented

The requested method is not implemented. The caller may wish to revert to a fallback approach based on other methods.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BufferNotLargeEnough)

### BufferNotLargeEnough

Buffer is not large enough

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CannotCreateACanonicalMessageWithACapability)

### CannotCreateACanonicalMessageWithACapability

Cannot create a canonical message with a capability

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CannotSetAnyPointerFieldToAPrimitiveValue)

### CannotSetAnyPointerFieldToAPrimitiveValue

Cannot set AnyPointer field to a primitive value

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CantHandleNonStructInlineComposite)

### CantHandleNonStructInlineComposite

Don’t know how to handle non-STRUCT inline composite.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyBuffer)

### EmptyBuffer

Empty buffer

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptySlice)

### EmptySlice

Empty slice

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EnumValueOrUnionDiscriminantNotPresent)

### EnumValueOrUnionDiscriminantNotPresent([NotInSchema](https://docs.rs/struct.NotInSchema.html))

Enum value or union discriminant {} was not present in schema

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExistingListPointerIsNotByteSized)

### ExistingListPointerIsNotByteSized

Called get_writable_{data|text}_pointer() but existing list pointer is not byte-sized.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExistingListValueIsIncompatibleWithExpectedType)

### ExistingListValueIsIncompatibleWithExpectedType

Existing list value is incompatible with expected type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExistingPointerIsNotAList)

# lazy_auto_reconnect in capnp_rpc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/capnp-rpc/0.26.1/capnp_rpc/fn.lazy_auto_reconnect.html

## Expand description

Creates a new client that lazily connect and also reconnects when getting [ ErrorKind::Disconnected](https://docs.rs/capnp/0.26.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/capnp/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.Disconnected) errors.

For explanation of how this functions see: `auto_reconnect`

The main difference between [ auto_reconnect](https://docs.rs/fn.auto_reconnect.html) and this function is that while

[will call the closure immediately to get an inner client to wrap, this function starts out disconnected and only calls the closure to get the actual client when the capability is first used.](https://docs.rs/fn.auto_reconnect.html)

`auto_reconnect`

# kigumi-server 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-server/0.1.0

Headless HTTP layer (axum). Serves the integration surface from a model set: the OpenAPI spec, the model list, per-model UI contracts, and — when a database backend is provided — secured data endpoints that enforce the ACL + record-rule engine.

The server is agnostic of any module: a host wires its catalog in with
`kigumi_core::resolve_all_registered()` and its security policy, then calls [`router`] or
[`router_with_data`]. The core stays headless; this crate is optional.

# async_stream - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/async-stream/^0.3/

## Expand description

Asynchronous stream of elements.

Provides two macros, `stream!` and `try_stream!`, allowing the caller to
define asynchronous streams of elements. These are implemented using `async`
& `await` notation. This crate works without unstable features.

The `stream!` macro returns an anonymous type implementing the [ Stream](https://docs.rs/futures-core/*/futures_core/stream/trait.Stream.html)
trait. The

`Item` associated type is the type of the values yielded from the
stream. The `try_stream!` also returns an anonymous type implementing the
[trait, but the](https://docs.rs/futures-core/*/futures_core/stream/trait.Stream.html)

`Stream``Item` associated type is `Result<T, Error>`. The
`try_stream!` macro supports using `?` notation as part of the
implementation.[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

A basic stream yielding numbers. Values are yielded using the `yield`
keyword. The stream block must return `()`.

```
use async_stream::stream;
use futures_util::pin_mut;
use futures_util::stream::StreamExt;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let s = stream! {
        for i in 0..3 {
            yield i;
        }
    };
    pin_mut!(s); // needed for iteration
    while let Some(value) = s.next().await {
        println!("got {}", value);
    }
}
```
Streams may be returned by using `impl Stream<Item = T>`:

```
use async_stream::stream;
use futures_core::stream::Stream;
use futures_util::pin_mut;
use futures_util::stream::StreamExt;
fn zero_to_three() -> impl Stream<Item = u32> {
    stream! {
        for i in 0..3 {
            yield i;
        }
    }
}
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let s = zero_to_three();
    pin_mut!(s); // needed for iteration
    while let Some(value) = s.next().await {
        println!("got {}", value);
    }
}
```
Streams may be implemented in terms of other streams - `async-stream` provides `for await`
syntax to assist with this:

```
use async_stream::stream;
use futures_core::stream::Stream;
use futures_util::pin_mut;
use futures_util::stream::StreamExt;
fn zero_to_three() -> impl Stream<Item = u32> {
    stream! {
        for i in 0..3 {
            yield i;
        }
    }
}
fn double<S: Stream<Item = u32>>(input: S)
    -> impl Stream<Item = u32>
{
    stream! {
        for await value in input {
            yield value * 2;
        }
    }
}
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let s = double(zero_to_three());
    pin_mut!(s); // needed for iteration
    while let Some(value) = s.next().await {
        println!("got {}", value);
    }
}
```
Rust try notation (`?`) can be used with the `try_stream!` macro. The `Item`
of the returned stream is `Result` with `Ok` being the value yielded and
`Err` the error type returned by `?`.

```
use tokio::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use async_stream::try_stream;
use futures_core::stream::Stream;
use std::io;
use std::net::SocketAddr;
fn bind_and_accept(addr: SocketAddr)
    -> impl Stream<Item = io::Result<TcpStream>>
{
    try_stream! {
        let mut listener = TcpListener::bind(addr).await?;
        loop {
            let (stream, addr) = listener.accept().await?;
            println!("received on {:?}", addr);
            yield stream;
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

The `stream!` and `try_stream!` macros are implemented using proc macros.
The macro searches the syntax tree for instances of `yield $expr` and
transforms them into `sender.send($expr).await`.

The stream uses a lightweight sender to send values from the stream
implementation to the caller. When entering the stream, an `Option<T>` is
stored on the stack. A pointer to the cell is stored in a thread local and
`poll` is called on the async block. When `poll` returns.
`sender.send(value)` stores the value that cell and yields back to the
caller.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [stream](https://docs.rs/macro.stream.html)
- Asynchronous stream
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_stream.html)- stream
- Asynchronous fallible stream

---

# axum - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/axum/^0.7/

## Expand description

axum is a web application framework that focuses on ergonomics and modularity.

[§](https://docs.rs#high-level-features)High-level features

- Route requests to handlers with a macro-free API.
- Declaratively parse requests using extractors.
- Simple and predictable error handling model.
- Generate responses with minimal boilerplate.
- Take full advantage of the `tower``tower-http`

In particular, the last point is what sets `axum` apart from other frameworks.
`axum` doesn’t have its own middleware system but instead uses
[ tower::Service](https://docs.rs/tower-service/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tower_service/trait.Service.html). This means

`axum` gets timeouts, tracing, compression,
authorization, and more, for free. It also enables you to share middleware with
applications written using [or](http://crates.io/crates/hyper)

`hyper`[.](http://crates.io/crates/tonic)

`tonic`[§](https://docs.rs#compatibility)Compatibility

axum is designed to work with [tokio](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.41.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/index.html) and [hyper](https://docs.rs/hyper/1.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hyper/index.html). Runtime and
transport layer independence is not a goal, at least for the time being.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

The “Hello, World!” of axum is:

```
use axum::{
    routing::get,
    Router,
};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    // build our application with a single route
    let app = Router::new().route("/", get(|| async { "Hello, World!" }));
    // run our app with hyper, listening globally on port 3000
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:3000").await.unwrap();
    axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}
```
Note using `#[tokio::main]` requires you enable tokio’s `macros` and `rt-multi-thread` features
or just `full` to enable all features (`cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread`).

[§](https://docs.rs#routing)Routing

[ Router](https://docs.rs/struct.Router.html) is used to set up which paths goes to which services:

```
use axum::{Router, routing::get};
// our router
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/", get(root))
    .route("/foo", get(get_foo).post(post_foo))
    .route("/foo/bar", get(foo_bar));
// which calls one of these handlers
async fn root() {}
async fn get_foo() {}
async fn post_foo() {}
async fn foo_bar() {}
```
See [ Router](https://docs.rs/struct.Router.html) for more details on routing.

[§](https://docs.rs#handlers)Handlers

In axum a “handler” is an async function that accepts zero or more
[“extractors”](https://docs.rs/extract/index.html) as arguments and returns something that
can be converted [into a response](https://docs.rs/response/index.html).

Handlers are where your application logic lives and axum applications are built by routing between handlers.

See [ handler](https://docs.rs/handler/index.html) for more details on handlers.

[§](https://docs.rs#extractors)Extractors

An extractor is a type that implements [ FromRequest](https://docs.rs/extract/trait.FromRequest.html) or

[. Extractors are how you pick apart the incoming request to get the parts your handler needs.](https://docs.rs/extract/trait.FromRequestParts.html)

`FromRequestParts````
use axum::extract::{Path, Query, Json};
use std::collections::HashMap;
// `Path` gives you the path parameters and deserializes them.
async fn path(Path(user_id): Path<u32>) {}
// `Query` gives you the query parameters and deserializes them.
async fn query(Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>) {}
// Buffer the request body and deserialize it as JSON into a
// `serde_json::Value`. `Json` supports any type that implements
// `serde::Deserialize`.
async fn json(Json(payload): Json<serde_json::Value>) {}
```
See [ extract](https://docs.rs/extract/index.html) for more details on extractors.

[§](https://docs.rs#responses)Responses

Anything that implements [ IntoResponse](https://docs.rs/response/trait.IntoResponse.html) can be returned from handlers.

```
use axum::{
    body::Body,
    routing::get,
    response::Json,
    Router,
};
use serde_json::{Value, json};
// `&'static str` becomes a `200 OK` with `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`
async fn plain_text() -> &'static str {
    "foo"
}
// `Json` gives a content-type of `application/json` and works with any type
// that implements `serde::Serialize`
async fn json() -> Json<Value> {
    Json(json!({ "data": 42 }))
}
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/plain_text", get(plain_text))
    .route("/json", get(json));
```
See [ response](https://docs.rs/response/index.html) for more details on building responses.

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

axum aims to have a simple and predictable error handling model. That means it is simple to convert errors into responses and you are guaranteed that all errors are handled.

See [ error_handling](https://docs.rs/error_handling/index.html) for more details on axum’s
error handling model and how to handle errors gracefully.

[§](https://docs.rs#middleware)Middleware

There are several different ways to write middleware for axum. See
[ middleware](https://docs.rs/middleware/index.html) for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#sharing-state-with-handlers)Sharing state with handlers

It is common to share some state between handlers. For example, a pool of database connections or clients to other services may need to be shared.

The three most common ways of doing that are:

- Using the `State`
- Using request extensions
- Using closure captures

```
use axum::{
    extract::State,
    routing::get,
    Router,
};
use std::sync::Arc;
struct AppState {
    // ...
}
let shared_state = Arc::new(AppState { /* ... */ });
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/", get(handler))
    .with_state(shared_state);
async fn handler(
    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
) {
    // ...
}
```
You should prefer using [ State](https://docs.rs/extract/struct.State.html) if possible since it’s more type safe. The downside is that
it’s less dynamic than request extensions.

See [ State](https://docs.rs/extract/struct.State.html) for more details about accessing state.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-request-extensions)Using request extensions

Another way to extract state in handlers is using [ Extension](https://docs.rs/struct.Extension.html) as
layer and extractor:

```
use axum::{
    extract::Extension,
    routing::get,
    Router,
};
use std::sync::Arc;
struct AppState {
    // ...
}
let shared_state = Arc::new(AppState { /* ... */ });
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/", get(handler))
    .layer(Extension(shared_state));
async fn handler(
    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,
) {
    // ...
}
```
The downside to this approach is that you’ll get runtime errors
(specifically a `500 Internal Server Error` response) if you try and extract
an extension that doesn’t exist, perhaps because you forgot to add the
middleware or because you’re extracting the wrong type.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-closure-captures)Using closure captures

State can also be passed directly to handlers using closure captures:

```
use axum::{
    Json,
    extract::{Extension, Path},
    routing::{get, post},
    Router,
};
use std::sync::Arc;
use serde::Deserialize;
struct AppState {
    // ...
}
let shared_state = Arc::new(AppState { /* ... */ });
let app = Router::new()
    .route(
        "/users",
        post({
            let shared_state = Arc::clone(&shared_state);
            move |body| create_user(body, shared_state)
        }),
    )
    .route(
        "/users/:id",
        get({
            let shared_state = Arc::clone(&shared_state);
            move |path| get_user(path, shared_state)
        }),
    );
async fn get_user(Path(user_id): Path<String>, state: Arc<AppState>) {
    // ...
}
async fn create_user(Json(payload): Json<CreateUserPayload>, state: Arc<AppState>) {
    // ...
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct CreateUserPayload {
    // ...
}
```
The downside to this approach is that it’s a little more verbose than using
[ State](https://docs.rs/extract/struct.State.html) or extensions.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-tokios-task_local-macro)Using [tokio’s ](https://docs.rs/tokio/1/tokio/macro.task_local.html)`task_local` macro:

`task_local` macroThis allows to share state with `IntoResponse` implementations.

```
use axum::{
    extract::Request,
    http::{header, StatusCode},
    middleware::{self, Next},
    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
    routing::get,
    Router,
};
use tokio::task_local;
#[derive(Clone)]
struct CurrentUser {
    name: String,
}
task_local! {
    pub static USER: CurrentUser;
}
async fn auth(req: Request, next: Next) -> Result<Response, StatusCode> {
    let auth_header = req
        .headers()
        .get(header::AUTHORIZATION)
        .and_then(|header| header.to_str().ok())
        .ok_or(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)?;
    if let Some(current_user) = authorize_current_user(auth_header).await {
        // State is setup here in the middleware
        Ok(USER.scope(current_user, next.run(req)).await)
    } else {
        Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
    }
}
async fn authorize_current_user(auth_token: &str) -> Option<CurrentUser> {
    Some(CurrentUser {
        name: auth_token.to_string(),
    })
}
struct UserResponse;
impl IntoResponse for UserResponse {
    fn into_response(self) -> Response {
        // State is accessed here in the IntoResponse implementation
        let current_user = USER.with(|u| u.clone());
        (StatusCode::OK, current_user.name).into_response()
    }
}
async fn handler() -> UserResponse {
    UserResponse
}
let app: Router = Router::new()
    .route("/", get(handler))
    .route_layer(middleware::from_fn(auth));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#building-integrations-for-axum)Building integrations for axum

Libraries authors that want to provide [ FromRequest](https://docs.rs/extract/trait.FromRequest.html),

[, or](https://docs.rs/extract/trait.FromRequestParts.html)

`FromRequestParts`[implementations should depend on the](https://docs.rs/response/trait.IntoResponse.html)

`IntoResponse`[crate, instead of](http://crates.io/crates/axum-core)

`axum-core``axum` if
possible. [contains core types and traits and is less likely to receive breaking changes.](http://crates.io/crates/axum-core)

`axum-core`[§](https://docs.rs#required-dependencies)Required dependencies

To use axum there are a few dependencies you have to pull in as well:

```
[dependencies]
axum = "<latest-version>"
tokio = { version = "<latest-version>", features = ["full"] }
tower = "<latest-version>"
```
The `"full"` feature for tokio isn’t necessary but it’s the easiest way to get started.

Tower isn’t strictly necessary either but helpful for testing. See the testing example in the repo to learn more about testing axum apps.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The axum repo contains [a number of examples](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/tree/main/examples) that show how to put all the
pieces together.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

axum uses a set of [feature flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html#the-features-section) to reduce the amount of compiled and
optional dependencies.

The following optional features are available:

| Name | Description | Default? |
|---|---|---|
| `http1` | Enables hyper’s `http1`feature | Yes |
| `http2` | Enables hyper’s `http2`feature | No |
| `json` | Enables the type and some similar convenience functionality`Json` | Yes |
| `macros` | Enables optional utility macros | No |
| `matched-path` | Enables capturing of every request’s router path and the extractor`MatchedPath` | Yes |
| `multipart` | Enables parsing `multipart/form-data`requests with`Multipart` | No |
| `original-uri` | Enables capturing of every request’s original URI and the extractor`OriginalUri` | Yes |
| `tokio` | Enables `tokio`as a dependency and`axum::serve`,`SSE`and`extract::connect_info`types. | Yes |
| `tower-log` | Enables `tower`’s`log`feature | Yes |
| `tracing` | Log rejections from built-in extractors | Yes |
| `ws` | Enables WebSockets support via `extract::ws` | No |
| `form` | Enables the `Form`extractor | Yes |
| `query` | Enables the `Query`extractor | Yes |

# genpdf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/genpdf/^0.2/

## Expand description

User-friendly PDF generator written in pure Rust.

`genpdf` is a high-level PDF generator built ontop of [ printpdf](https://docs.rs/printpdf) and

[. It takes care of the page layout and text alignment and renders a document tree into a PDF document. All of its dependencies are written in Rust, so you don’t need any pre-installed libraries or tools.](https://docs.rs/rusttype)

`rusttype`[§](https://docs.rs#quickstart)Quickstart

To generate a PDF document, create an instance of the [ Document](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html) struct and add

[implementations to it. Then call the](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html)

`Element`[method to render the document and to write it to a file.](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.render_to_file)

`Document::render_to_file````
// Load a font from the file system
let font_family = genpdf::fonts::from_files("./fonts", "LiberationSans", None)
    .expect("Failed to load font family");
// Create a document and set the default font family
let mut doc = genpdf::Document::new(font_family);
// Change the default settings
doc.set_title("Demo document");
// Customize the pages
let mut decorator = genpdf::SimplePageDecorator::new();
decorator.set_margins(10);
doc.set_page_decorator(decorator);
// Add one or more elements
doc.push(genpdf::elements::Paragraph::new("This is a demo document."));
// Render the document and write it to a file
doc.render_to_file("output.pdf").expect("Failed to write PDF file");
```
For a complete example with all supported elements, see the [ examples/demo.rs](https://git.sr.ht/~ireas/genpdf-rs/tree/master/examples/demo.rs) file that
generates

[this PDF document](https://genpdf-rs.ireas.org/examples/demo.pdf).

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

A [ Document](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html) consists of a

[that renders the added elements, a](https://docs.rs/elements/struct.LinearLayout.html)

`LinearLayout`[instance that keeps track of the loaded fonts and a collection of default values for the text style and the page layout.](https://docs.rs/fonts/struct.FontCache.html)

`FontCache`When creating a [ Document](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html) instance, you always have to set the default font family that
will be used for the document.  You can load additional fonts with the

[method.](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.load_font_family)

`Document::load_font_family`The style of a shape or text can be set using the [ Style](https://docs.rs/style/struct.Style.html) struct.  The style is inherited
within the document tree.  You can set the style of an element by wrapping it in a

[(see the](https://docs.rs/elements/StyledElement.html)

`StyledElement`[method) or – for text elements – with a](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html#tymethod.styled)

`Element::styled`[.](https://docs.rs/style/struct.StyledString.html)

`StyledString`For an overview of the available elements, see the [ elements](https://docs.rs/elements/) module.  You can also
create custom elements by implementing the

[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html)

`Element`The actual PDF document is generated from the elements that have been added to the document
once you call the [ Document::render](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.render) or

[methods. For details on the rendering process, see the next section.](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.render_to_file)

`Document::render_to_file`In `genpdf`, all lengths are measured in millimeters.  The only exceptions are font sizes that
are measured in points.  The [ Mm](https://docs.rs/struct.Mm.html) newtype struct is used for all lengths, and the

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Position.html)

`Position`[types are used to describe points and rectangles in the PDF document.](https://docs.rs/struct.Size.html)

`Size`[§](https://docs.rs#rendering-process)Rendering Process

The rendering process is started by calling the [ Document::render](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.render) or

[methods. You can only render a document once. Before the rendering starts, the PDF document is created and all loaded fonts are embedded into the document.](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.render_to_file)

`Document::render_to_file`The elements are then rendered by calling the [ Element::render](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html#tymethod.render) method of the root element,
a

[. This element will then call the](https://docs.rs/elements/struct.LinearLayout.html)

`LinearLayout``render` methods of the elements stored
in the layout, and so on.The [ Element::render](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html#tymethod.render) method receives the following arguments:

- *context*is the context for the rendering process, see- `Context`- `FontCache`- `Style`
- *area*is a view on the area of the current page that can be used by the element.
- *style*is the- `Style`- `Document`- `StyledElement`

The `render` method tries to render the entire element in the provided area.  The returned
[ RenderResult](https://docs.rs/struct.RenderResult.html) stores the size of the area that has actually been used to render the
element.  If the element did not fit into the provided area, the

`has_more` field of the
[is set to](https://docs.rs/struct.RenderResult.html)

`RenderResult``true`.  This causes the `Document` to add a new page to the PDF
document and then call the `render` method again with an area of the new page.  This is
repeated until all elements have been rendered completely, that means until all elements return
a [with](https://docs.rs/struct.RenderResult.html)

`RenderResult``has_more == false`.Elements may print to the provided area using the methods of the [ Area](https://docs.rs/render/struct.Area.html) struct, or by
calling the

`render` method of other elements, or both.Every new page is prepared by calling the document’s [ PageDecorator](https://docs.rs/trait.PageDecorator.html) (if set).  This
decorator can add a margin to the page, print a header, a footer, or perform other tasks.

The render process is cancelled if an `Element` returns an error, or if no content has been
rendered to a newly created page.  This indicates that an element does not fit on a clear page
and can’t even be rendered partially, so the rendering process is cancelled.

As the [ Element::render](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html#tymethod.render) method is called repeatedly until the complete element has been
rendered, the element has to keep track of the content that has already been rendered.  As
there is only one rendering process per document, elements may discard data that has been
rendered and that is no longer needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#low-level-interface)Low-Level Interface

The [ render](https://docs.rs/render/) module contains a low-level interface for creating PDF files.  It keeps track
of page sizes and layers and has utility methods for easier text and shape rendering.  But it
does not provide support for measuring the size of rendered text or for laying out elements.
If possible, you should always try to use

`genpdf`’s high-level interface and implement the
[trait if you want to customize a document instead of using the low-level interface directly.](https://docs.rs/trait.Element.html)

`Element`[§](https://docs.rs#known-issues)Known Issues

- Currently, `genpdf`adds all loaded fonts to the PDF document, even if they are not used.`printpdf`then adds all available glyphs for these fonts to the document, even if they are not used in the document. This increases the file size by 100–200 KiB per font (500–1000 KiB per font family). Until this is fixed, you can pass the generated file through`ps2pdf`to significantly reduce its size. Alternatively, you can use a built-in font if you don’t need any characters that are not supported by the[Windows-1252](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows-1252)encoding.

- A PDF document.
- [Margins](https://docs.rs/struct.Margins.html)
- The margins of an area, measured in millimeters.

- A length measured in millimeters.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/struct.Position.html)

- A rotation in degrees clock-wise in range [-180.0, 180.0] inclusive.

# kigumi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Kigumi core: the inspectable metamodel + the module versioning model.

Difference from Odoo (see `docs/ANALISI_ODOO19.md`): a model definition is NOT
a class synthesized at runtime with `type()`, but inspectable static data;
extension is a VERIFIED MERGE, not a global monkey-patch; dependencies between
modules have verified VERSION RANGES (Odoo does not have them — see `docs/VERSIONING.md`).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [inventory](https://docs.rs/inventory/0.3.24/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/inventory/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Acl](https://docs.rs/struct.Acl.html)
- Model-level access grant for one group (the `ir.model.access`analog).
- [AclRegistration](https://docs.rs/struct.AclRegistration.html)
- Registration of a module’s ACLs (emitted by `register_acls!`). Compile-time security data; M6 adds a DB-backed loader on top, but the in-code registry stays the bootstrap/default source.
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionInput.html)- Input
- Read-only view of the record an action runs on (its current stored values), with typed accessors.
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionOutcome.html)- Outcome
- What an action produces: field updates to apply, plus an optional “assign field = next_value(code)” directive resolved by the persistence layer (which can call the sequence engine).
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of an action by (model, name), emitted by `register_action!`.`groups`(if non-empty) restricts who may run it, on top of the model’s Write ACL + record rules.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputeInput.html)- Input
- Read-only view of a record (its own fields + its One2many children), passed to a compute
function. Same-record computes read `int`/`float`/…; aggregate computes read`children`/`sum_float`.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputeRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a compute function by name (emitted by `register_compute!`).
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html)
- A single leaf condition `field <op> value`.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/struct.ConstraintRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a constraint on a model, evaluated when any of `fields`is written (an empty`fields`runs on every write). Emitted by`register_constraint!`.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/struct.ConstraintViolation.html)- Violation
- A constraint violation: the failing rule’s message plus the fields the rule DECLARED as its triggers — the fields a form should highlight. Empty for an unconditional (whole-record) rule.
- [Ctx](https://docs.rs/struct.Ctx.html)
- Evaluation context: who is acting, and whether checks are bypassed.
- [Delegated](https://docs.rs/struct.DelegatedField.html)- Field
- A field a child transparently exposes from its `_inherits`parent: the parent’s`FieldDef``via`FK column the read subquery / write UPDATE pivots on.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalTable.html)- Table
- A model whose table is owned OUTSIDE the metamodel (e.g. the auth subsystem’s `kigumi_user`, or a SQL view): registered so it is resolved/served like any model, but EXCLUDED from migration — the metamodel never creates or alters its table. Odoo’s`_auto = False`. Emitted by`register_external!`.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldBuilder.html)- Builder
- Fluent builder for a single condition.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldDef.html)- Def
- Definition of a single field.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldExtension.html)- Extension
- Registration of a field extension (emitted by `#[extend]`).
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldGroup.html)- Group
- A titled group of scalar fields, laid out in two columns. `title`is optional (a lead group with no heading is common for the identity fields).
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldGroupRegistration.html)- Group - Registration
- Field-level access restriction (D6 / Odoo’s `Field.groups`): the groups required to access one`model.field`. Registered out-of-band (emitted by`#[field(groups = "...")]`) so it adds no column to the metamodel and no churn to existing`FieldDef`literals — the same side-registry pattern as external tables. Read AND write are gated by the same set, at the DB boundary.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldSlot.html)- Slot
- A field placed in a group. `full`makes it span both columns — use it for relations, long text (Html), images, and the primary name.
- [Form](https://docs.rs/struct.FormView.html)- View
- A model’s form layout. Emitted by `register_view!`.
- [Inherits](https://docs.rs/struct.InheritsRegistration.html)- Registration
- Delegation inheritance (Odoo’s `_inherits`):`model`carries a required Many2one`via`to`parent`and transparently exposes the parent’s stored scalar fields (read via the FK, written through to the parent). Emitted by`#[model(inherits = "parent", via = "fk")]`. The`via`FK is an ordinary field the model declares — this only records the delegation, so no`ModelDescriptor`/`FieldDef`churn.
- [Mailed](https://docs.rs/struct.MailedRegistration.html)- Registration
- A model that opts INTO the mail subsystem (chatter): it gains a thread of `mail.message`s, followers and activities, addressed by the polymorphic`(res_model, res_id)`link. Emitted by`register_mailed!`. Unlike Odoo’s 5118-line`mail.thread`mixin, this is a one-line compile-time marker the framework iterates — to gate the chatter API and to clean up the thread on delete.
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/struct.MigrationTarget.html)- Target
- One model to migrate, with the owning module’s name + version (for the migration ledger).
- [Model](https://docs.rs/struct.ModelDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Descriptor of a model as defined by ONE module (the “base”).
- [Model](https://docs.rs/struct.ModelRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a base model (emitted by `#[model]`).
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleDep.html)- Dep
- Dependency on another module, with a SemVer version constraint (e.g. “^1.2”).
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleManifest.html)- Manifest
- Manifest of a module. Declarative data, validated at build/install time.
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a module manifest (emitted by `register_module!`).`crate_path`is the Rust module path of the registering crate (`module_path!()`), used to map a model — whose own registration carries`module_path!()`— back to its owning manifest (name + version).
- [Notebook](https://docs.rs/struct.NotebookPage.html)- Page
- A notebook page (tab) below the sheet, usually a One2many relation or grouped secondary fields.
- [Readonly](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadonlyFieldRegistration.html)- Field - Registration
- A stored field declared read-only: shown in the UI contract as `readonly`and rejected by the write path (like a computed field), even though it is not computed. Emitted by`#[field(readonly)]`. Used for materialized values a service method maintains (e.g. on-hand) — visible, never hand-edited.
- [Record](https://docs.rs/struct.RecordRule.html)- Rule
- Row-level rule (the `ir.rule`analog).`groups`empty = global (applies to everyone).
- [Record](https://docs.rs/struct.RecordRuleRegistration.html)- Rule - Registration
- Registration of a module’s record rules (emitted by `register_rules!`).
- [Related](https://docs.rs/struct.RelatedRegistration.html)- Registration
- A related field (Odoo `related=`): a NON-stored, read-only mirror of a value reached by following a relational`path`(e.g.`order_id.currency_id`). Registered out-of-band (emitted by`#[field(related = "...")]`) so it adds no column to the metamodel — the value is resolved at read time by a correlated subquery over the path. The field’s declared kind must match the path target.
- [Report](https://docs.rs/struct.ReportRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a report by (model, name), emitted by `register_report!`.`name`is the URL segment (e.g. “quotation”);`title`is the human label used in the contract and the download filename.
- [Resolved](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolvedModel.html)- Model
- RESOLVED descriptor: base + all extensions merged and validated. This is the point — absent in Odoo — where the final definition is materializable.
- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/struct.SequenceRegistration.html)- Registration
- A module’s document-numbering sequence (emitted by `register_sequence!`): declared next to the action that consumes it, ensured at migrate — an existing sequence keeps its counter.`module`is diagnostic only (a cross-module code collision is reported with both names).
- [Sql](https://docs.rs/struct.Sql.html)
- Compiled SQL: a boolean expression plus its ordered bound parameters.
- [Tracked](https://docs.rs/struct.TrackedFieldRegistration.html)- Field - Registration
- A field whose changes are tracked in the chatter (Odoo’s `tracking=True`). When a write changes it on a mailed model, the write path records a`notification`message + a typed`mail.tracking`row (old → new). Emitted by`#[field(tracked)]`. Compile-time, not runtime`track_visibility`.
- [Transient](https://docs.rs/struct.TransientRegistration.html)- Registration
- A model whose rows are ephemeral (Odoo’s `TransientModel`): a wizard scratchpad with its own table, served and secured like any model, but periodically garbage-collected by age. Emitted by`register_transient!`. A transient model declares a nullable`create_date Datetime`; migration gives that column a`DEFAULT now()`so every insert is timestamped and the GC cron can reclaim it.
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/struct.WizardContext.html)- Context
- The records a wizard is opened against (Odoo’s `active_model`/`active_id`/`active_ids`context).
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/struct.WizardRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a wizard (emitted by `register_wizard!`): binds a transient model to its`default_get`. The model must also be`register_transient!`-marked (so its rows are GC’d).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.Domain.html)
- A filter expression. Combine with `and`/`or`/`not`.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.DomainError.html)- Error
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldKind.html)- Kind
- Logical type of a field. From this we derive the SQL type, UI widget, and API type.
- [Operation](https://docs.rs/enum.Operation.html)
- A CRUD operation subject to access control.
- [Operator](https://docs.rs/enum.Operator.html)
- [Resolution](https://docs.rs/enum.ResolutionError.html)- Error
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/enum.RuleDomain.html)- Domain
- The domain source of a `RecordRule``Static`(a thunk, because a`Domain``Owned`, holding a domain parsed at load time. The engine treats both identically — only where the domain comes from differs, so static and DB rules merge into one list with no special-casing.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html)
- A scalar (or list) literal used on the right-hand side of a condition.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Model](https://docs.rs/trait.Model.html)
- Implemented by every model. In the walking skeleton it is written by hand;
in phase 2 it is generated by the `#[model]`proc-macro.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [action_](https://docs.rs/fn.action_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered action by model + name.
- [actions_](https://docs.rs/fn.actions_for.html)- for
- All actions registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can render its action buttons).
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_access.html)- access
- Returns true if `ctx`may perform`op`on`model`. Access is granted if ANY of the user’s groups grants it (union semantics, like Odoo). Superuser is always allowed.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_compat.html)- compat
- Verifies that `manifest`is compatible with the provided framework version. This is the check Odoo does NOT do: there a “19.0” module runs (or breaks) on any 19.x.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_constraints.html)- constraints
- Runs the model’s constraints over a just-written record (`values`+ its`children`).`changed`is the set of written field names, or`None`on create (every constraint runs). A constraint runs when it is unconditional (empty`fields`), on create, or when one of its trigger`fields`was written. Returns the first violation (message + the rule’s declared fields), which the caller maps to a typed error that rolls back the tx.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_fn.html)- fn
- Looks up a registered compute function by its declared name.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_on_read.html)- on_ - read
- Evaluates the model’s NON-stored computed fields (Odoo `compute=`without`store=True`) over a record’s`values`at READ time, returning the (name, value) pairs to inject into the projection. These have no column and are never written — they are derived on every read. Same-record:`children`is empty, so a function reads the record’s own scalar fields plus any related / delegated values already present in`values`(both are read alongside the columns), not its One2many children.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_stored.html)- stored
- Fills `values`with the result of each stored computed field whose function is registered, given the record’s own fields and its One2many`children`(for aggregate computes). Computes from a snapshot taken BEFORE writing any result, so computes read the inputs (chained compute-on-compute is not ordered — out of scope).
- [computed_](https://docs.rs/fn.computed_fields.html)- fields
- Names of the model’s stored computed fields that have a registered function.
- [delegated_](https://docs.rs/fn.delegated_fields.html)- fields
- The fields `model`delegates to its`_inherits`parent (empty if it is not a child). Each is read via the parent through the`via`FK; the child does NOT have a column for it. A name the child also declares (an intentional shadow, e.g.`product.product.active`over`product.template.active`) is excluded — the child’s own column wins and the parent’s is not delegated.
- [external_](https://docs.rs/fn.external_tables.html)- tables
- Names of models whose tables the metamodel must NOT migrate (owned externally).
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_accessible.html)- accessible
- Whether `ctx`may access (read or write)`model.field`. Default-allow when the field has no group restriction; superuser always allowed; otherwise the caller must be in at least one required group. Mirrors Odoo, which gates read and write by the same`Field.groups`set at the ORM boundary.
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_is_readonly.html)- is_ - readonly
- Whether `model`.`field`is declared`#[field(readonly)]`.
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_required_groups.html)- required_ - groups
- The groups required to access `model.field`, or None when the field is unrestricted. Delegation- aware (`_inherits`): a restriction on an inherited field lives on the PARENT model, so when the field is not restricted directly on`model`we fall back to the parent — otherwise an inherited field would expose its restricted value through the child (read/order/filter). Recurses the chain. Shadow-aware: a name the child declares as its OWN column (e.g.`product.product.active`over`product.template.active`) does NOT borrow the parent’s restriction — only genuinely delegated fields fall back, so a group added to the parent never silently gates the child’s own column.
- [has_](https://docs.rs/fn.has_constraints.html)- constraints
- True iff the model has any registered constraint — a cheap gate before the in-transaction re-read
that `check_constraints`
- [has_](https://docs.rs/fn.has_read_computes.html)- read_ - computes
- True iff the model has any NON-stored computed field (a cheap gate before doing the extra decode
that `compute_on_read`
- [inherits_](https://docs.rs/fn.inherits_of.html)- of
- The `(parent, via)`a model delegates to, or None if it is not an`_inherits`child.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_mailed.html)- mailed
- Whether `model`has a mail thread (chatter enabled).
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_transient.html)- transient
- Whether `model`is transient (its rows are garbage-collected by age).
- [json_](https://docs.rs/fn.json_string.html)- string
- JSON-escapes `s`and wraps it in double quotes. Shared by domain and UI-contract serialization so every string in the emitted JSON is escaped consistently (no broken-out quotes).
- [mailed_](https://docs.rs/fn.mailed_models.html)- models
- Names of all models that opted into the mail subsystem.
- [migration_](https://docs.rs/fn.migration_plan.html)- plan
- The full migration plan, TOPOLOGICALLY SORTED by Many2one FK dependencies (a model’s FK targets — e.g. res.currency/res.partner for res.company — are created before the referencing table). Self-references are ignored (a table may reference itself in its own CREATE); a genuine FK cycle between two tables is an error. Ties break by (module dependency order, model name) for determinism. Each target carries its owning module’s name + version for the migration ledger.
- [module_](https://docs.rs/fn.module_closure.html)- closure
- A module plus its full transitive dependency closure, in dependency order (dependencies first) —
the set to install when installing `name`. Errors if`name`(or a dependency) is not a linked module, or the module graph is invalid.
- [module_](https://docs.rs/fn.module_of.html)- of
- The name of the module that owns `model`, via the model’s registration crate_path → manifest mapping (the same hook`migration_plan`uses). Used to gate migration/serving by installed module.
- [record_](https://docs.rs/fn.record_rule_domain.html)- rule_ - domain
- Combines the record rules applicable to (`op`,`model`,`ctx`) into a single restricting`Domain``None`when nothing restricts (superuser, or no applicable rule).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_acls.html)- acls
- All ACLs registered across linked modules (the union a server enforces).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_group_names.html)- group_ - names
- Distinct group names referenced by any registered ACL or record rule — the catalog’s known
groups (the source for seeding the read-only `res.groups`list). Sorted, deterministic.
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_model_names.html)- model_ - names
- Names of all models registered in the catalog (sorted, deterministic).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_rules.html)- rules
- All record rules registered across linked modules.
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_sequences.html)- sequences
- All sequences registered across linked modules.
- [related_](https://docs.rs/fn.related_path.html)- path
- The relational path a related field mirrors, or None if `field`is not a related field.
- [report_](https://docs.rs/fn.report_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered report by model + name.
- [reports_](https://docs.rs/fn.reports_for.html)- for
- All reports registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can offer its “Print” buttons).
- [resolve](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve.html)
- Merges the base with the module extensions. Conflicts are errors.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_all_registered.html)- all_ - registered
- Resolves every registered model (base + extensions). The bridge from the catalog to a server or any consumer that needs the full set of models.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_module_set.html)- module_ - set
- Resolves a set of modules: checks framework compatibility, that every dependency exists with a satisfying SemVer version, that there are no duplicate names and no cycles. Returns the modules in dependency (topological) order — what Odoo computes implicitly.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_modules.html)- modules
- Resolves every module registered in the catalog: framework compatibility, dependency
version ranges, no duplicates, no cycles — returning them in dependency order.
The validation `resolve_module_set`does is exactly what Odoo’s`depends`cannot express.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_registered.html)- registered
- Resolves a model from the CATALOG: registered base + all auto-registered extensions, merged (with conflict checks) and validated. No wiring: modules auto-register.
- [tracked_](https://docs.rs/fn.tracked_fields.html)- fields
- The names of `model`’s tracked fields (changes recorded in the chatter on write).
- [transient_](https://docs.rs/fn.transient_models.html)- models
- Names of all transient (ephemeral / wizard) models.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_depends.html)- depends
- Verifies that each `depends`points to an existing field (first segment of the path). Antidote to Odoo’s silent N+1: a broken dependency is an error, not a runtime bug.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_depends_with_extra.html)- depends_ - with_ - extra
- Like `validate_depends``extra`lists additional valid first-segment names — the`_inherits`delegated fields, which have no column on`m`yet are readable on the record (so an on-read compute may depend on, e.g., the inherited`name`). The registry passes the delegated names here.
- [view_](https://docs.rs/fn.view_for.html)- for
- The registered form view for `model`, if any (else the frontend applies a smart default layout).
- [wizard_](https://docs.rs/fn.wizard_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered wizard by model name.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Action](https://docs.rs/type.ActionFn.html)- Fn
- A registered action: a pure transition function. Guards (e.g. “only a draft”) live in the body
and return `Err(message)`to refuse the transition.
- [Children](https://docs.rs/type.Children.html)
- One2many children grouped by the o2m field name (each child is its own field→value map).
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/type.ComputeFn.html)- Fn
- A registered compute function.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/type.ConstraintFn.html)- Fn
- A constraint over a just-written record: returns `Err(message)`to reject (and roll back) the write.
- [Report](https://docs.rs/type.ReportFn.html)- Fn
- Renders a record — with its inlined One2many children, exactly as `find_one_secured`returns it — to a complete HTML document. Pure: no DB access and no recompute; it reads only the fields present.
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/type.WizardDefaultGet.html)- Default - Get
- Computes a wizard’s seed field values from the context (Odoo’s `default_get`). Pure in v1 (no DB reads); DB-backed defaults are a later extension done by a dedicated open service method.

# kigumi_schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-schema/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

The projections: from a `ResolvedModel` to Postgres DDL and an agnostic UI contract (JSON).

Same source of truth → multiple outputs. The UI contract carries visibility/readonly rules as
a portable [ Domain](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/domain/enum.Domain.html) JSON AST — the frontend evaluates them client-side from data, never an
eval’d string, and they are the SAME domains the server compiles to SQL.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldRule.html)- Rule
- A dynamic UI rule bound to a field: when `domain`holds for a record, the field becomes invisible/readonly. The domain is a thunk because a`Domain`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [openapi](https://docs.rs/fn.openapi.html)
- Builds a pretty-printed OpenAPI 3.1 document describing `models`.
- [pg_](https://docs.rs/fn.pg_add_column_type.html)- add_ - column_ - type
- The column TYPE plus its foreign-key reference for an additive `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`— the subset of`to_ddl`’s column spec WITHOUT NOT NULL / UNIQUE / CHECK / DEFAULT, so it is safe to add to a populated table (the column is simply NULL on existing rows; required-ness is enforced at the write layer).`None`for kinds with no own column (One2many / Many2many).
- [pg_](https://docs.rs/fn.pg_column_type.html)- column_ - type
- Postgres SQL type for a field with a column.
The Postgres column type for a field kind — used by `to_ddl`and by the runtime custom-field`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`. Empty string for kinds that have no own column (One2many/Many2many).
- [to_ddl](https://docs.rs/fn.to_ddl.html)
- Generates the `CREATE TABLE`. Non-stored computed fields and one2many produce no columns.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_ui_contract.html)- ui_ - contract
- Agnostic UI contract: JSON consumable by ANY frontend. Computed fields are readonly; dynamic
`invisible_when`/`readonly_when`rules are emitted as portable domain ASTs.

# kigumi_storage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-storage/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Content-addressed blob storage. Binary attachments live behind an interchangeable [ BlobStore](https://docs.rs/trait.BlobStore.html),
keyed by the sha256 of their content: identical bytes dedupe to one immutable object, and every

`put` re-verifies the hash so the content-address invariant is enforced, never trusted.v1 ships [ FsBlobStore](https://docs.rs/struct.FsBlobStore.html) (files at

`<root>/ab/cd/<hash>`). The API is buffered (a whole blob is held
in memory); streaming for very large blobs (the backup/restore path) is a later enhancement —
attachments are single files of modest size. `S3BlobStore` / `DbBlobStore` are out of v1.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FsBlob](https://docs.rs/struct.FsBlobStore.html)- Store
- Filesystem blob store: immutable, deduplicated files at `<root>/ab/cd/<hash>`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Blob](https://docs.rs/enum.BlobError.html)- Error
- Errors a blob store can return.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Blob](https://docs.rs/trait.BlobStore.html)- Store
- An interchangeable, content-addressed binary store.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [sha256_](https://docs.rs/fn.sha256_hex.html)- hex
- The sha256 of `bytes`as lowercase hex — the content address used as a blob key.

# rust_decimal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust_decimal/^1/

## Expand description

A Decimal number implementation written in pure Rust suitable for financial calculations that require significant integral and fractional digits with no round-off errors.

The binary representation consists of a 96 bit integer number, a scaling factor used to specify the decimal fraction and
a 1 bit sign. Because of this representation, trailing zeros are preserved and may be exposed when in string form. These
can be truncated using the `normalize` or `round_dp` functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#installing)Installing

`$ cargo add rust_decimal`Alternatively, you can edit your `Cargo.toml` directly and run `cargo update`:

```
[dependencies]
rust_decimal = "1.42"
```
To enable macro support, you can enable the `macros` feature:

`$ cargo add rust_decimal --features macros`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Decimal numbers can be created in a few distinct ways. The easiest and most efficient method of creating a Decimal is to use the macro:

```
// Import via use rust_decimal_macros or use the `macros` feature to import at the crate level
// `use rust_decimal_macros::dec;`
// or
// `use rust_decimal::dec;`
let number = dec!(-1.23) + dec!(3.45);
assert_eq!(number, dec!(2.22));
assert_eq!(number.to_string(), "2.22");
```
Alternatively you can also use one of the Decimal number convenience
functions ([see the docs](https://docs.rs/rust_decimal/) for more details):

```
// Using the prelude can help importing trait based functions (e.g. core::str::FromStr).
use rust_decimal::prelude::*;
// Using an integer followed by the decimal points
let scaled = Decimal::new(202, 2);
assert_eq!("2.02", scaled.to_string());
// From a 128 bit integer
let balance = Decimal::from_i128_with_scale(5_897_932_384_626_433_832, 2);
assert_eq!("58979323846264338.32", balance.to_string());
// From a string representation
let from_string = Decimal::from_str("2.02").unwrap();
assert_eq!("2.02", from_string.to_string());
// From a string representation in a different base
let from_string_base16 = Decimal::from_str_radix("ffff", 16).unwrap();
assert_eq!("65535", from_string_base16.to_string());
// From scientific notation
let sci = Decimal::from_scientific("9.7e-7").unwrap();
assert_eq!("0.00000097", sci.to_string());
// Using the `Into` trait
let my_int: Decimal = 3_i32.into();
assert_eq!("3", my_int.to_string());
// Using the raw decimal representation
let pi = Decimal::from_parts(1_102_470_952, 185_874_565, 1_703_060_790, false, 28);
assert_eq!("3.1415926535897932384626433832", pi.to_string());
// If the `macros` feature is enabled, it also allows for the `dec!` macro
let amount = dec!(25.12);
assert_eq!("25.12", amount.to_string());
```
Once you have instantiated your `Decimal` number you can perform calculations with it just like any other number:

```
use rust_decimal::prelude::*; // Includes the `dec` macro when feature specified
let amount = dec!(25.12);
let tax_percentage = dec!(0.085);
let total = amount + (amount * tax_percentage).round_dp(2);
assert_eq!(total, dec!(27.26));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

**Behavior / Functionality**

**Database**

**Serde**

- [serde-float](https://docs.rs#serde-float)
- [serde-str](https://docs.rs#serde-str)
- [serde-arbitrary-precision](https://docs.rs#serde-arbitrary-precision)
- [serde-with-float](https://docs.rs#serde-with-float)
- [serde-with-str](https://docs.rs#serde-with-str)
- [serde-with-arbitrary-precision](https://docs.rs#serde-with-arbitrary-precision)

[§](https://docs.rs#align16)`align16`

Forces `Decimal`’s alignment to 16 bytes (128 bits). This is identical to `u128` and `i128`’s alignment on x86 platforms.

[§](https://docs.rs#borsh)`borsh`

Enables [Borsh](https://borsh.io/) serialization for `Decimal`.

[§](https://docs.rs#bytemuck)`bytemuck`

Enables [bytemuck](https://github.com/Lokathor/bytemuck) support by deriving `Pod` and `Zeroable` for `Decimal`. This also activates the `c-repr` feature since `Pod` requires `repr(C)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#c-repr)`c-repr`

Forces `Decimal` to use `[repr(C)]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#db-postgres)`db-postgres`

Enables a PostgreSQL communication module. It allows for reading and writing the `Decimal`
type by transparently serializing/deserializing into the `NUMERIC` data type within PostgreSQL.

[§](https://docs.rs#db-tokio-postgres)`db-tokio-postgres`

Enables the tokio postgres module allowing for async communication with PostgreSQL.

[§](https://docs.rs#db-diesel-postgres)`db-diesel-postgres`

Enable [ diesel](https://diesel.rs) PostgreSQL support.

[§](https://docs.rs#db-diesel-mysql)`db-diesel-mysql`

Enable [ diesel](https://diesel.rs) MySQL support.

[§](https://docs.rs#legacy-ops)`legacy-ops`

**Warning:** This is deprecated and will be removed from a future versions.

As of `1.10` the algorithms used to perform basic operations have changed which has benefits of significant speed
improvements.
To maintain backwards compatibility this can be opted out of by enabling the `legacy-ops` feature.

[§](https://docs.rs#macros)`macros`

The `macros` feature enables a compile time macro `dec` to be available at both the crate root, and via prelude.

This parses the input at compile time and converts it to an optimized `Decimal` representation. Invalid inputs will
cause a compile time error.

Any Rust number format is supported, including scientific notation and alternate bases.

```
use rust_decimal::prelude::*;
assert_eq!(dec!(1.23), Decimal::new(123, 2));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#maths)`maths`

The `maths` feature enables additional complex mathematical functions such as `pow`, `ln`, `enf`, `exp` etc.
Documentation detailing the additional functions can be found on the
[ MathematicalOps](https://docs.rs/rust_decimal/latest/rust_decimal/trait.MathematicalOps.html) trait.

Please note that `ln` and `log10` will panic on invalid input with `checked_ln` and `checked_log10` the preferred
functions
to curb against this. When the `maths` feature was first developed the library would instead return `0` on invalid
input. To re-enable this
non-panicking behavior, please use the feature: `maths-nopanic`.

[§](https://docs.rs#ndarray)`ndarray`

Enables arithmetic operations using [ ndarray](https://github.com/rust-ndarray/ndarray) on arrays of

`Decimal`.[§](https://docs.rs#proptest)`proptest`

Enables a [ proptest](https://github.com/proptest-rs/proptest) strategy to generate values for Rust Decimal.

[§](https://docs.rs#rand)`rand`

Implements `rand::distributions::Distribution<Decimal>` to allow the creation of random instances.

Note: When using `rand::Rng` trait to generate a decimal between a range of two other decimals, the scale of the
randomly-generated
decimal will be the same as the scale of the input decimals (or, if the inputs have different scales, the higher of the
two).

[§](https://docs.rs#rkyv)`rkyv`

Enables [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv) serialization for `Decimal`. In order to avoid breaking changes, this is
currently locked at version `0.7`.

Supports rkyv’s safe API when the `rkyv-safe` feature is enabled as well.

If `rkyv` support for versions `0.8` of greater is desired, `rkyv`’
s [remote derives](https://rkyv.org/derive-macro-features/remote-derive.html) should be used instead. See
`examples/rkyv-remote`.

[§](https://docs.rs#rocket-traits)`rocket-traits`

Enable support for Rocket forms by implementing the `FromFormField` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-fuzz)`rust-fuzz`

Enable `rust-fuzz` support by implementing the `Arbitrary` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-float)`serde-float`

Note:This feature applies float serialization/deserialization rules as the default method for handling`Decimal`numbers. See also the`serde-with-*`features for greater flexibility.

Enable this so that JSON serialization of `Decimal` types are sent as a float instead of a string (default).

e.g. with this turned on, JSON serialization would output:

```
{
  "value": 1.234
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#serde-str)`serde-str`

Note:This feature applies string serialization/deserialization rules as the default method for handling`Decimal`numbers. See also the`serde-with-*`features for greater flexibility.

This is typically useful for `bincode` or `csv` like implementations.

Since `bincode` does not specify type information, we need to ensure that a type hint is provided in order to
correctly be able to deserialize. Enabling this feature on its own will force deserialization to use `deserialize_str`
instead of `deserialize_any`.

If, for some reason, you also have `serde-float` enabled then this will use `deserialize_f64` as a type hint. Because
converting to `f64` *loses* precision, it’s highly recommended that you do NOT enable this feature when working with
`bincode`. That being said, this will only use 8 bytes so is slightly more efficient in terms of storage size.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-arbitrary-precision)`serde-arbitrary-precision`

Note:This feature applies arbitrary serialization/deserialization rules as the default method for handling`Decimal`numbers. See also the`serde-with-*`features for greater flexibility.

This is used primarily with `serde_json` and consequently adds it as a “weak dependency”. This supports the
`arbitrary_precision` feature inside `serde_json` when parsing decimals.

This is recommended when parsing “float” looking data as it will prevent data loss.

Please note, this currently serializes numbers in a float like format by default, which can be an unexpected
consequence. For greater
control over the serialization format, please use the `serde-with-arbitrary-precision` feature.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-with-float)`serde-with-float`

Enable this to access the module for serializing `Decimal` types to a float. This can be used in `struct` definitions
like so:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FloatExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::float")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct OptionFloatExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::float_option")]
    value: Option<Decimal>,
}
```
Alternatively, if only the serialization feature is desired (e.g. to keep flexibility while deserialization):

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FloatExample {
    #[serde(serialize_with = "rust_decimal::serde::float::serialize")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#serde-with-str)`serde-with-str`

Enable this to access the module for serializing `Decimal` types to a `String`. This can be used in `struct` definitions
like so:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StrExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::str")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct OptionStrExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::str_option")]
    value: Option<Decimal>,
}
```
This feature isn’t typically required for serialization however can be useful for deserialization purposes since it does not require a type hint. Consequently, you can force this for just deserialization by:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StrExample {
    #[serde(deserialize_with = "rust_decimal::serde::str::deserialize")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#serde-with-arbitrary-precision)`serde-with-arbitrary-precision`

Enable this to access the module for deserializing `Decimal` types using the `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` feature.
This can be used in `struct` definitions like so:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ArbitraryExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::arbitrary_precision")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct OptionArbitraryExample {
    #[serde(with = "rust_decimal::serde::arbitrary_precision_option")]
    value: Option<Decimal>,
}
```
An unexpected consequence of this feature is that it will serialize as a float like number. To prevent this, you can
target the struct to only deserialize with the `arbitrary_precision` feature:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ArbitraryExample {
    #[serde(deserialize_with = "rust_decimal::serde::arbitrary_precision::deserialize")]
    value: Decimal,
}
```
This will ensure that serialization still occurs as a string.

Please see the `examples` directory for more information regarding `serde_json` scenarios.

[§](https://docs.rs#std)`std`

Enable `std` library support. This is enabled by default, however in the future will be opt in. For now, to
support `no_std`
libraries, this crate can be compiled with `--no-default-features`.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm)`wasm`

Enable [ wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen) support which makes

`Decimal` compatible with the
`wasm_bindgen` attribute macro and exposes the following methods across boundaries:- `fromNumber()`/- `toNumber()`— convert between- `Decimal`and the primitive- `number`type.
- `fromString()`/- `toString()`— convert between- `Decimal`and a string representation.

[§](https://docs.rs#building)Building

Please refer to the [Build document](https://github.com/paupino/rust-decimal/blob/master/BUILD.md) for more information on building and testing Rust Decimal.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-rust-compiler-version)Minimum Rust Compiler Version

The current *minimum* compiler version is `1.67.1` which was released on `2023-02-09`.

This library maintains support for rust compiler versions that are 4 minor versions away from the current stable rust
compiler version.
For example, if the current stable compiler version is `1.50.0` then we will guarantee support up to and
including `1.46.0`.
Of note, we will only update the minimum supported version if and when required.

[§](https://docs.rs#comparison-to-other-decimal-implementations)Comparison to other Decimal implementations

During the development of this library, there were various design decisions made to ensure that decimal calculations would be quick, accurate and efficient. Some decisions, however, put limitations on what this library can do and ultimately what it is suitable for. One such decision was the structure of the internal decimal representation.

This library uses a mantissa of 96 bits made up of three 32-bit unsigned integers with a fourth 32-bit unsigned integer to represent the scale/sign (similar to the C and .NET Decimal implementations). This structure allows us to make use of algorithmic optimizations to implement basic arithmetic; ultimately this gives us the ability to squeeze out performance and make it one of the fastest implementations available. The downside of this approach however is that the maximum number of significant digits that can be represented is roughly 28 base-10 digits (29 in some cases).

While this constraint is not an issue for many applications (e.g. when dealing with money), some applications may require a higher number of significant digits to be represented. Fortunately, there are alternative implementations that may be worth investigating, such as:

If you have further questions about the suitability of this library for your project, then feel free to either start a
[discussion](https://github.com/paupino/rust-decimal/discussions) or open
an [issue](https://github.com/paupino/rust-decimal/issues) and we’ll
do our best to help.

- [serde](https://docs.rs/serde/index.html)- `serde`and (- `serde-with-arbitrary-precision`or- `serde-with-float`or- `serde-with-str`)

# hmac - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hmac/^0.12/

## Expand description

Generic implementation of Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC).

To use it you will need a cryptographic hash function implementation which
implements the [ digest](https://docs.rs/digest) crate traits. You can find compatible crates
(e.g.

[) in the](https://docs.rs/sha2)

`sha2`[repository.](https://github.com/RustCrypto/hashes)

`RustCrypto/hashes`This crate provides two HMAC implementation [ Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html) and

[. The first one is a buffered wrapper around block-level](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`[. Internally it uses efficient state representation, but works only with hash functions which expose block-level API and consume blocks eagerly (e.g. it will not work with the BLAKE2 family of hash functions). On the other hand,](https://docs.rs/struct.HmacCore.html)

`HmacCore`[is a bit less efficient memory-wise, but works with all hash functions which implement the](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`[trait.](https://docs.rs/digest)

`Digest`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Let us demonstrate how to use HMAC using the SHA-256 hash function.

In the following examples [ Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html) is interchangeable with

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`To get authentication code:

```
use sha2::Sha256;
use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};
use hex_literal::hex;
// Create alias for HMAC-SHA256
type HmacSha256 = Hmac<Sha256>;
let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(b"my secret and secure key")
    .expect("HMAC can take key of any size");
mac.update(b"input message");
// `result` has type `CtOutput` which is a thin wrapper around array of
// bytes for providing constant time equality check
let result = mac.finalize();
// To get underlying array use `into_bytes`, but be careful, since
// incorrect use of the code value may permit timing attacks which defeats
// the security provided by the `CtOutput`
let code_bytes = result.into_bytes();
let expected = hex!("
    97d2a569059bbcd8ead4444ff99071f4
    c01d005bcefe0d3567e1be628e5fdcd9
");
assert_eq!(code_bytes[..], expected[..]);
```
To verify the message:

```
let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(b"my secret and secure key")
    .expect("HMAC can take key of any size");
mac.update(b"input message");
let code_bytes = hex!("
    97d2a569059bbcd8ead4444ff99071f4
    c01d005bcefe0d3567e1be628e5fdcd9
");
// `verify_slice` will return `Ok(())` if code is correct, `Err(MacError)` otherwise
mac.verify_slice(&code_bytes[..]).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#block-and-input-sizes)Block and input sizes

Usually it is assumed that block size is larger than output size. Due to the generic nature of the implementation, this edge case must be handled as well to remove potential panic. This is done by truncating hash output to the hash block size if needed.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [digest](https://docs.rs/digest/0.10.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/digest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Hmac](https://docs.rs/struct.HmacCore.html)- Core
- Generic core HMAC instance, which operates over blocks.
- [Simple](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)- Hmac
- Simplified HMAC instance able to operate over hash functions which do not expose block-level API and hash functions which process blocks lazily (e.g. BLAKE2).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Mac](https://docs.rs/trait.Mac.html)
- Convenience wrapper trait covering functionality of Message Authentication algorithms.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html)
- Generic HMAC instance.

# sha2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sha2/^0.10/

## Expand description

An implementation of the [SHA-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) cryptographic hash algorithms.

There are 6 standard algorithms specified in the SHA-2 standard: [ Sha224](https://docs.rs/type.Sha224.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha256.html)

`Sha256`[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512_224.html)

`Sha512_224`[,](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512_256.html)

`Sha512_256`[, and](https://docs.rs/type.Sha384.html)

`Sha384`[.](https://docs.rs/type.Sha512.html)

`Sha512`Algorithmically, there are only 2 core algorithms: SHA-256 and SHA-512. All other algorithms are just applications of these with different initial hash values, and truncated to different digest bit lengths. The first two algorithms in the list are based on SHA-256, while the last four are based on SHA-512.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#one-shot-api)One-shot API

```
use hex_literal::hex;
use sha2::{Sha256, Digest};
let result = Sha256::digest(b"hello world");
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9
")[..]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#incremental-api)Incremental API

```
use hex_literal::hex;
use sha2::{Sha256, Sha512, Digest};
// create a Sha256 object
let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
// write input message
hasher.update(b"hello world");
// read hash digest and consume hasher
let result = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9
")[..]);
// same for Sha512
let mut hasher = Sha512::new();
hasher.update(b"hello world");
let result = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("
    309ecc489c12d6eb4cc40f50c902f2b4d0ed77ee511a7c7a9bcd3ca86d4cd86f
    989dd35bc5ff499670da34255b45b0cfd830e81f605dcf7dc5542e93ae9cd76f
")[..]);
```
Also see [RustCrypto/hashes](https://github.com/RustCrypto/hashes) readme.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [digest](https://docs.rs/digest/0.10.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/digest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Sha256](https://docs.rs/struct.Sha256VarCore.html)- VarCore
- Core block-level SHA-256 hasher with variable output size.
- [Sha512](https://docs.rs/struct.Sha512VarCore.html)- VarCore
- Core block-level SHA-512 hasher with variable output size.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Digest](https://docs.rs/trait.Digest.html)
- Convenience wrapper trait covering functionality of cryptographic hash functions with fixed output size.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compress256](https://docs.rs/fn.compress256.html)- `compress`
- Raw SHA-256 compression function.
- [compress512](https://docs.rs/fn.compress512.html)- `compress`
- Raw SHA-512 compression function.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Sha224](https://docs.rs/type.Sha224.html)
- SHA-224 hasher.
- [Sha256](https://docs.rs/type.Sha256.html)
- SHA-256 hasher.

- SHA-384 hasher.
