# sqlx - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sqlx/^0.8/

## Expand description

The async SQL toolkit for Rust, built with ❤️ by [the LaunchBadge team](https://www.launchbadge.com).

See our [README](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/README.md) to get started or [browse our example projects](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/examples).
Have a question? [Check our FAQ](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/FAQ.md) or [open a discussion](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/discussions/new?category=q-a).

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-support)Runtime Support

SQLx supports both the [Tokio](https://www.tokio.rs) and [async-std](https://www.async.rs) runtimes.

You choose which runtime SQLx uses by default by enabling one of the following features:

- `runtime-async-std`
- `runtime-tokio`

The `runtime-actix` feature also exists but is an alias of `runtime-tokio`.

If more than one runtime feature is enabled, the Tokio runtime is used if a Tokio context exists on the current
thread, i.e. [ tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current()](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/runtime/struct.Handle.html#method.try_current) returns

`Ok`; `async-std` is used otherwise.Note that while SQLx no longer produces a compile error if zero or multiple runtime features are enabled,
which is useful for libraries building on top of it,
**the use of nearly any async function in the API will panic without at least one runtime feature enabled**.

The chief exception is the SQLite driver, which is runtime-agnostic, including its integration with the query macros.
However, `SqlitePool`*does* require runtime support for timeouts and spawning
internal management tasks.

[§](https://docs.rs#tls-support)TLS Support

For securely communicating with SQL servers over an untrusted network connection such as the internet, you can enable Transport Layer Security (TLS) by enabling one of the following features:

- `tls-native-tls`: Enables the- `native-tls`- SecureTransport on macOS.
- SChannel on Windows.
- OpenSSL on all other platforms.

- `tls-rustls`: Enables the- [rustls](https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/)backend, a cross-platform TLS library.- Only supports TLS revisions 1.2 and 1.3.
- If you get `HandshakeFailure`errors when using this feature, it likely means your database server does not support these newer revisions. This might be resolved by enabling or switching to the`tls-native-tls`feature.
- rustls supports several providers of cryptographic primitives. The default
(enabled when you use the `tls-rustls`feature or`tls-rustls-ring`) is the`ring`provider, which has fewer build-time dependencies but also has fewer features. Alternatively, you can use`tls-rustls-aws-lc-rs`to use the`aws-lc-rs`provider, which enables additional cipher suite support at the cost of more onerous build requirements (depending on platform support).

If more than one TLS feature is enabled, the `tls-native-tls` feature takes precedent so that it is only necessary to enable
it to see if it resolves the `HandshakeFailure` error without disabling `tls-rustls`.

Consult the user manual for your database to find the TLS versions it supports.

If your connection configuration requires a TLS upgrade but TLS support was not enabled, the connection attempt will return an error.

The legacy runtime+TLS combination feature flags are still supported, but for forward-compatibility, use of the separate runtime and TLS feature flags is recommended.

# tempfile - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempfile/^3/

## Expand description

This is a library for creating temporary files and directories that are automatically deleted when no longer referenced (i.e., on drop).

- Use `tempfile()``std::fs::File`
- Use `NamedTempFile::new()`*named*temporary file that can be referred to its path.
- Use `tempdir()`
- Use `spooled_tempfile()`

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

This crate provides several approaches to creating temporary files and directories.
[ tempfile()](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) relies on the OS to remove the temporary file once the last handle is closed.

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`[both rely on Rust destructors for cleanup.](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[§](https://docs.rs#resource-leaking)Resource Leaking

`tempfile` will (almost) never fail to cleanup temporary resources. However `TempDir` and
`NamedTempFile` will fail if their destructors don’t run. This is because `tempfile` relies on
the OS to cleanup the underlying file, while `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on rust
destructors to do so. Destructors may fail to run if the process exits through an unhandled
signal interrupt (like `SIGINT`), or if the instance is declared statically (like with
[ lazy_static](https://github.com/rust-lang-nursery/lazy-static.rs/issues/62)), among other possible reasons.

[§](https://docs.rs#unexpected-file-deletion)Unexpected File Deletion

Most operating systems periodically clean up temporary files that haven’t been accessed recently
(often on the order of multiple days). This issue does not affect unnamed temporary files but
can invalidate the paths associated with named temporary files on Unix-like systems because the
temporary file can be unlinked from the filesystem while still open and in-use. See the
[temporary file cleaner](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners) section for more security implications.

[§](https://docs.rs#security)Security

This section discusses security issues relevant to Unix-like operating systems that use shared temporary directories by default. Importantly, it’s not relevant for Windows or macOS as both operating systems use private per-user temporary directories by default.

Applications can mitigate the issues described below by using [ env::override_temp_dir](https://docs.rs/env/fn.override_temp_dir.html) to
change the default temporary directory but should do so if and only if default the temporary
directory (

[) is unsuitable (is world readable, world writable, managed by a temporary file cleaner, etc.).](https://docs.rs/env/fn.temp_dir.html)

`env::temp_dir`[§](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners)Temporary File Cleaners

In the presence of pathological temporary file cleaner, relying on file paths is unsafe because a temporary file cleaner could delete the temporary file which an attacker could then replace.

This isn’t an issue for [ tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) as it doesn’t rely on file paths. However,

[and temporary directories](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`*do*rely on file paths for

*some*operations. See the security documentation on the

[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[types for more information.](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`Mitigation:

- This is rarely an issue for short-lived files as temporary file cleaners usually only remove temporary files that haven’t been modified or accessed within many (10-30) days.
- Very long lived temporary files should be placed in directories not managed by temporary file cleaners.

[§](https://docs.rs#access-permissions)Access Permissions

Temporary *files* created with this library are private by default on all operating systems.
However, temporary *directories* are created with the default permissions and will therefore be
world-readable by default unless the user has changed their umask and/or default temporary
directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#denial-of-service)Denial of Service

If the file-name randomness ([ Builder::rand_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.rand_bytes)) is too small and/or this crate is built
without the

`getrandom` feature, it may be possible for an attacker to predict the random file
names chosen by this library, preventing temporary file creation by creating temporary files
with these predicted file names. By default, this library mitigates this denial of service
attack by:- Defaulting to 6 random characters per temporary file forcing an attacker to create billions of files before random collisions are expected (at which point you probably have larger problems).
- Re-seeding the random filename generator from system randomness after 3 failed attempts to
create temporary a file (when the `getrandom`feature is enabled as it is by default on all major platforms).

[§](https://docs.rs#early-drop-pitfall)Early drop pitfall

Because `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on their destructors for cleanup, this can lead
to an unexpected early removal of the directory/file, usually when working with APIs which are
generic over `AsRef<Path>`. Consider the following example:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::process::Command;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let temp_dir = tempdir()?;
// Spawn the `touch` command inside the temporary directory and collect the exit status
// Note that `temp_dir` is **not** moved into `current_dir`, but passed as a reference
let exit_status = Command::new("touch").arg("tmp").current_dir(&temp_dir).status()?;
assert!(exit_status.success());
```
This works because a reference to `temp_dir` is passed to `current_dir`, resulting in the
destructor of `temp_dir` being run after the `Command` has finished execution. Moving the
`TempDir` into the `current_dir` call would result in the `TempDir` being converted into
an internal representation, with the original value being dropped and the directory thus
being deleted, before the command can be executed.

The `touch` command would fail with an `No such file or directory` error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a temporary file and write some data into it:

```
use tempfile::tempfile;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file = tempfile()?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
```
Create a named temporary file and open an independent file handle:

```
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
use std::io::{Write, Read};
let text = "Brian was here. Briefly.";
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new()?;
// Re-open it.
let mut file2 = file1.reopen()?;
// Write some test data to the first handle.
file1.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
// Read the test data using the second handle.
let mut buf = String::new();
file2.read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
assert_eq!(buf, text);
```
Create a temporary directory and add a file to it:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let dir = tempdir()?;
let file_path = dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
let mut file = File::create(file_path)?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
// By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
// been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
// the directory will still be deleted when `dir` goes out
// of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
// succeeded.
drop(file);
dir.close()?;
```

- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)

# tower - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower/^0.5/

## Expand description

`async fn(Request) -> Result<Response, Error>`

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tower is a library of modular and reusable components for building robust networking clients and servers.

Tower provides a simple core abstraction, the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) trait, which
represents an asynchronous function taking a request and returning either a
response or an error. This abstraction can be used to model both clients and
servers.

Generic components, like [ timeout](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html),

[rate limiting](https://docs.rs/limit/rate/index.html), and

[load balancing](https://docs.rs/balance/index.html), can be modeled as

[s that wrap some inner service and apply additional behavior before or after the inner service is called. This allows implementing these components in a protocol-agnostic, composable way. Typically, such services are referred to as](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`*middleware*.

An additional abstraction, the [ Layer](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html) trait, is used to compose
middleware with

[s. If a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[can be thought of as an asynchronous function from a request type to a response type, a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[is a function taking a](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[of one type and returning a](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[of a different type. The](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[type is used to add middleware to a service by composing it with multiple](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceBuilder.html)

`ServiceBuilder`[s.](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[§](https://docs.rs#the-tower-ecosystem)The Tower Ecosystem

Tower is made up of the following crates:

- `tower`
- `tower-service`
- `tower-layer`
- `tower-test`

Since the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) and

[traits are important integration points for all libraries using Tower, they are kept as stable as possible, and breaking changes are made rarely. Therefore, they are defined in separate crates,](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[and](https://crates.io/crates/tower-service)

`tower-service`[. This crate contains re-exports of those core traits, implementations of commonly-used middleware, and](https://crates.io/crates/tower-layer)

`tower-layer`[utilities](https://docs.rs/trait.ServiceExt.html)for working with

[s and](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

`Service`[s. Finally, the](https://docs.rs/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[crate provides tools for testing programs using Tower.](https://crates.io/crates/tower-test)

`tower-test`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Tower provides an abstraction layer, and generic implementations of various
middleware. This means that the `tower` crate on its own does *not* provide
a working implementation of a network client or server. Instead, Tower’s
[ Service trait](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) provides an integration point between
application code, libraries providing middleware implementations, and
libraries that implement servers and/or clients for various network
protocols.

Depending on your particular use case, you might use Tower in several ways:

-
**Implementing application logic**for a networked program. You might use the`Service`[provided by this crate](https://docs.rs#modules)and by other libraries to add functionality to clients and servers provided by one or more protocol implementations.
-
**Implementing middleware**to add custom behavior to network clients and servers in a reusable manner. This might be general-purpose middleware (and if it is, please consider releasing your middleware as a library for other Tower users!) or application-specific behavior that needs to be shared between multiple clients or servers.
-
**Implementing a network protocol**. Libraries that implement network protocols (such as HTTP) can depend on`tower-service`to use the`Service``Service``Service`Additionally, when a network protocol requires functionality already provided by existing Tower middleware, a protocol implementation might use Tower middleware internally, as well as as an integration point.

[§](https://docs.rs#library-support)Library Support

A number of third-party libraries support Tower and the [ Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html) trait.
The following is an incomplete list of such libraries:

- `hyper`
- `tonic`- [gRPC-over-HTTP/2](https://grpc.io)implementation built on top of- `hyper`- [here](https://github.com/hyperium/tonic/tree/master/examples/src/tower)for examples of using- `tonic`
- `warp`- [here](https://docs.rs/warp/0.2.5/warp/fn.service.html)for details on using- `warp`
- `tower-lsp`- [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/)based on Tower.

If you’re the maintainer of a crate that supports Tower, we’d love to add
your crate to this list! Please [open a PR](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/compare) adding a brief description of
your library!

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting Started

If you’re brand new to Tower and want to start with the basics, we recommend you
check out some of our [guides](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/tree/master/guides).

The various middleware implementations provided by this crate are feature flagged, so that users can only compile the parts of Tower they need. By default, all the optional middleware are disabled.

To get started using all of Tower’s optional middleware, add this to your
`Cargo.toml`:

`tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["full"] }`Alternatively, you can only enable some features. For example, to enable
only the [ retry](https://docs.rs/retry/index.html) and

[middleware, write:](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html)

`timeout``tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["retry", "timeout"] }`See [here](https://docs.rs#modules) for a complete list of all middleware provided by
Tower.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-rust-versions)Supported Rust Versions

Tower will keep a rolling MSRV (minimum supported Rust version) policy of **at
least** 6 months. When increasing the MSRV, the new Rust version must have been
released at least six months ago. The current MSRV is 1.64.0.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [balance](https://docs.rs/balance/index.html)- `balance`
- Middleware that allows balancing load among multiple services.
- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `buffer`
- Middleware that provides a buffered mpsc channel to a service.
- [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html)
- Builder types to compose layers and services
- [discover](https://docs.rs/discover/index.html)- `discover`
- Service discovery
- [filter](https://docs.rs/filter/index.html)- `filter`
- Conditionally dispatch requests to the inner service based on the result of a predicate.
- [hedge](https://docs.rs/hedge/index.html)- `hedge`
- Pre-emptively retry requests which have been outstanding for longer than a given latency percentile.
- [layer](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html)
- A collection of `Layer`

- Tower middleware for limiting requests.
- [load](https://docs.rs/load/index.html)- `load`
- Service load measurement
- [load_](https://docs.rs/load_shed/index.html)- shed - `load-shed`
- Middleware for shedding load when inner services aren’t ready.
- [make](https://docs.rs/make/index.html)- `make`
- Trait aliases for Services that produce specific types of Responses.
- [ready_](https://docs.rs/ready_cache/index.html)- cache - `ready-cache`
- A cache of services
- [reconnect](https://docs.rs/reconnect/index.html)- `reconnect`
- Reconnect services when they fail.
- [retry](https://docs.rs/retry/index.html)- `retry`
- Middleware for retrying “failed” requests.
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/spawn_ready/index.html)- ready - `spawn-ready`
- When an underlying service is not ready, drive it to readiness on a background task.
- [steer](https://docs.rs/steer/index.html)- `steer`
- This module provides functionality to aid managing routing requests between `Service`
- [timeout](https://docs.rs/timeout/index.html)- `timeout`
- Middleware that applies a timeout to requests.
- [util](https://docs.rs/util/index.html)- `util`
- Various utility types and functions that are generally used with Tower.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- Creates new `Service`
- [Service](https://docs.rs/trait.Service.html)

- [Service](https://docs.rs/trait.ServiceExt.html)- Ext - `util`
- An extension trait for `Service`s that provides a variety of convenient adapters

# kigumi_server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-server/0.1.0/target-redirect/kigumi_server/

## Expand description

Headless HTTP layer (axum). Serves the integration surface from a model set: the OpenAPI spec, the model list, per-model UI contracts, and — when a database backend is provided — secured data endpoints that enforce the ACL + record-rule engine.

The server is agnostic of any module: a host wires its catalog in with
`kigumi_core::resolve_all_registered()` and its security policy, then calls [ router](https://docs.rs/fn.router.html) or

[. The core stays headless; this crate is optional.](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data.html)

`router_with_data`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FsBlob](https://docs.rs/struct.FsBlobStore.html)- Store
- Filesystem blob store: immutable, deduplicated files at `<root>/ab/cd/<hash>`.
- [Genpdf](https://docs.rs/struct.GenpdfRasterizer.html)- Rasterizer
- Renders the report engine’s structured HTML to a PDF with genpdf.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Rasterizer](https://docs.rs/trait.Rasterizer.html)
- Rasterizes a rendered HTML report into PDF bytes. The seam for PDF output: a concrete backend
(e.g. typst- or headless-Chromium-based) plugs in via `router_with_data_rasterized`. When none is configured the report endpoint serves HTML and answers`?format=pdf`with 501.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [access_](https://docs.rs/fn.access_fingerprint.html)- fingerprint
- A cheap content hash of the DB-backed ACL/rule rows (owned data, no leak). The poll loop compares
it across ticks and only reloads the policy when it changes — so out-of-band edits (the `kigumi acl/rule`CLI, direct SQL) go live without paying the load_*_static string leak on every tick.
- [refresh_](https://docs.rs/fn.refresh_access.html)- access
- Recomputes the effective access policy — compiled-in baseline ∪ DB overrides — and swaps it into
the live snapshots, so a runtime ACL/rule change takes effect without a restart. On a DB load error
it KEEPS the prior good snapshot (it does not degrade to baseline-only — that would silently drop a
live restricting rule) and returns `false`, so the caller can retry on the next tick. Returns`true`only when both halves reloaded. NB it leaks the DB rows’ identifier strings (load_*_static), so the poll loop and the mutation endpoints guard it behind`access_fingerprint`
- [refresh_](https://docs.rs/fn.refresh_custom_fields.html)- custom_ - fields
- Reloads the live custom-field map from the registry (after an add, and at startup).
- [refresh_](https://docs.rs/fn.refresh_view_overrides.html)- view_ - overrides
- Reloads the live view-override map from `ir_ui_view`(after a change, and at startup). Owned data, so unlike the access policy this is leak-free and can run on every poll tick unconditionally.
- [router](https://docs.rs/fn.router.html)
- Metadata-only router: OpenAPI spec, model list, UI contracts. No database.
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data.html)- with_ - data
- Full router: metadata routes plus secured CRUD data endpoints. `auth_secret`is the HS256 secret used to verify the`Authorization: Bearer <token>`of each data request into a`Ctx`. No PDF rasterizer is configured (report`?format=pdf`answers 501); see`router_with_data_rasterized`
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_dynamic.html)- with_ - data_ - dynamic
- Like `router_with_data`**live served catalog**:`installed`(a shared, mutable set of installed module names) gates which models are served, so installing/uninstalling a module via the`/api/modules/*`endpoints takes effect without restarting the process (the host passes the FULL linked catalog as`models`and keeps`installed`in sync with the DB). Used by`kigumi serve`.
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_dynamic_rasterized.html)- with_ - data_ - dynamic_ - rasterized
- Like `router_with_data_dynamic``?format=pdf`(None → 501).
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_rasterized.html)- with_ - data_ - rasterized
- Like `router_with_data``?format=pdf`(None → those requests get 501).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [AclState](https://docs.rs/type.AclState.html)
- The effective access policy, swappable at runtime. Held as an `Arc`snapshot behind an`RwLock`: a request clones the current snapshot (cheap refcount bump) and reads it without holding the lock across`.await`, while the poll loop and the mutation endpoints replace the snapshot wholesale — so a DB-backed ACL/rule added via the CLI or the`/api/_acl``/api/_rule`endpoints takes effect with no restart, the same “declarative, no recompile” property as runtime custom fields.
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/type.RuleState.html)- State

live restricting rule) and returns `false`, so the caller can retry on the next tick. Returns`true`only when both halves reloaded. NB it leaks the DB rows’ identifier strings (load_*_static), so the poll loop and the mutation endpoints guard it behind`access_fingerprint`
- [refresh_](https://docs.rs/fn.refresh_custom_fields.html)- custom_ - fields
- Reloads the live custom-field map from the registry (after an add, and at startup).
- [refresh_](https://docs.rs/fn.refresh_view_overrides.html)- view_ - overrides
- Reloads the live view-override map from `ir_ui_view`(after a change, and at startup). Owned data, so unlike the access policy this is leak-free and can run on every poll tick unconditionally.
- [router](https://docs.rs/fn.router.html)
- Metadata-only router: OpenAPI spec, model list, UI contracts. No database.
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data.html)- with_ - data
- Full router: metadata routes plus secured CRUD data endpoints. `auth_secret`is the HS256 secret used to verify the`Authorization: Bearer <token>`of each data request into a`Ctx`. No PDF rasterizer is configured (report`?format=pdf`answers 501); see`router_with_data_rasterized`
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_dynamic.html)- with_ - data_ - dynamic
- Like `router_with_data`**live served catalog**:`installed`(a shared, mutable set of installed module names) gates which models are served, so installing/uninstalling a module via the`/api/modules/*`endpoints takes effect without restarting the process (the host passes the FULL linked catalog as`models`and keeps`installed`in sync with the DB). Used by`kigumi serve`.
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_dynamic_rasterized.html)- with_ - data_ - dynamic_ - rasterized
- Like `router_with_data_dynamic``?format=pdf`(None → 501).
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_data_rasterized.html)- with_ - data_ - rasterized
- Like `router_with_data``?format=pdf`(None → those requests get 501).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [AclState](https://docs.rs/type.AclState.html)
- The effective access policy, swappable at runtime. Held as an `Arc`snapshot behind an`RwLock`: a request clones the current snapshot (cheap refcount bump) and reads it without holding the lock across`.await`, while the poll loop and the mutation endpoints replace the snapshot wholesale — so a DB-backed ACL/rule added via the CLI or the`/api/_acl``/api/_rule`endpoints takes effect with no restart, the same “declarative, no recompile” property as runtime custom fields.
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/type.RuleState.html)- State

[90](#90)fn parse_custom_kind(kind: &str) -> Option<FieldKind> {
[92](#92)    match kind {
[93](#93)        "text" => Some(FieldKind::Text),
[94](#94)        "integer" => Some(FieldKind::Integer),
[95](#95)        "float" => Some(FieldKind::Float),
[96](#96)        "decimal" => Some(FieldKind::Decimal { currency_field: None }),
[97](#97)        "bool" => Some(FieldKind::Bool),
[98](#98)        "date" => Some(FieldKind::Date),
[99](#99)        "datetime" => Some(FieldKind::Datetime),
[100](#100)        _ => None,
[101](#101)    }
[102](#102)}
[103](#103)
[104](#104)fn custom_field_def(cf: &CustomField) -> Option<FieldDef> {
[108](#108)    let leak = |s: &str| -> &'static str { Box::leak(s.to_string().into_boxed_str()) };
[109](#109)    let kind = match cf.kind.as_str() {
[110](#110)        "many2one" => FieldKind::Many2one { target: leak(cf.relation.as_deref()?) },
[111](#111)        other => parse_custom_kind(other)?,
[112](#112)    };
[113](#113)    Some(FieldDef {
[114](#114)        name: leak(&cf.name),
[115](#115)        label: leak(&cf.label),
[116](#116)        kind,
[117](#117)        required: cf.required,
[118](#118)        stored: true,
[119](#119)        compute: None,
[120](#120)        depends: &[],
[121](#121)        default: cf.default_value.as_deref().map(leak),
[122](#122)        unique: false,
[123](#123)        check: None,
[124](#124)    })
[125](#125)}

[133](#133)        }
[134](#134)    }

[165](#165)
[166](#166)fn apply_view_overrides(contract: &str, overrides: &[ViewOverride]) -> String {
[171](#171)    let mut v: Json2 = match serde_json::from_str(contract) {
[172](#172)        Ok(v) => v,
[173](#173)        Err(_) => return contract.to_string(),
[174](#174)    };
[175](#175)    let by_field: HashMap<&str, &ViewOverride> =
[176](#176)        overrides.iter().map(|o| (o.field.as_str(), o)).collect();
[177](#177)    let rewrite = |arr: &mut Vec<Json2>| {
[178](#178)        arr.retain(|item| {
[179](#179)            item.get("name")
[180](#180)                .and_then(|n| n.as_str())
[181](#181)                .and_then(|n| by_field.get(n))
[182](#182)                .map(|o| !o.invisible)
[183](#183)                .unwrap_or(true)
[184](#184)        });
[185](#185)        for item in arr.iter_mut() {
[186](#186)            let Some(name) = item.get("name").and_then(|n| n.as_str()).map(str::to_string) else {
[187](#187)                continue;
[188](#188)            };
[189](#189)            let Some(o) = by_field.get(name.as_str()) else { continue };
[190](#190)            let Some(obj) = item.as_object_mut() else { continue };
[191](#191)            if let Some(l) = &o.label {
[192](#192)                obj.insert("label".into(), Json2::String(l.clone()));
[193](#193)            }
[194](#194)            if let Some(w) = &o.widget {
[195](#195)                obj.insert("widget".into(), Json2::String(w.clone()));
[196](#196)            }
[197](#197)            if o.readonly {
[198](#198)                obj.insert("readonly".into(), Json2::Bool(true));
[199](#199)            }
[200](#200)            for (col, dom) in [("invisible_when", &o.invisible_when), ("readonly_when", &o.readonly_when)] {
[203](#203)                if let Some(d) = dom {
[204](#204)                    if let Ok(ast) = serde_json::from_str::<Json2>(d) {
[205](#205)                        obj.insert(col.into(), ast);
[206](#206)                    }
[207](#207)                }
[208](#208)            }
[209](#209)        }
[210](#210)    };
[211](#211)    if let Some(arr) = v.get_mut("fields").and_then(|f| f.as_array_mut()) {
[212](#212)        rewrite(arr);
[213](#213)    }
[214](#214)    if let Some(cols) =
[215](#215)        v.get_mut("list").and_then(|l| l.get_mut("columns")).and_then(|c| c.as_array_mut())
[216](#216)    {
[217](#217)        rewrite(cols);
[218](#218)    }
[219](#219)    v.to_string()
[220](#220)}

[243](#243)    async fn reload_access(&self, before: u64) {
[247](#247)        if access_fingerprint(&self.db).await != before {

[252](#252)
[253](#253)pub async fn refresh_access(acls: &AclState, rules: &RuleState, db: &Db) -> bool {
[261](#261)    let mut ok = true;
[262](#262)    match db.load_acls_static().await {
[263](#263)        Ok(db_a) => {
[264](#264)            let mut a = registered_acls();
[265](#265)            a.extend(db_a);
[266](#266)            if let Ok(mut w) = acls.write() {
[267](#267)                *w = Arc::from(a);
[268](#268)            }
[269](#269)        }
[270](#270)        Err(_) => ok = false,
[272](#272)    }
[273](#273)    match db.load_rules_static().await {
[274](#274)        Ok(db_r) => {
[275](#275)            let mut r = registered_rules();
[276](#276)            r.extend(db_r);
[277](#277)            if let Ok(mut w) = rules.write() {
[278](#278)                *w = Arc::from(r);
[279](#279)            }
[280](#280)        }
[281](#281)        Err(_) => ok = false,
[282](#282)    }
[283](#283)    ok
[284](#284)}
[285](#285)
[286](#286)pub async fn access_fingerprint(db: &Db) -> u64 {
[290](#290)    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
[291](#291)    let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
[292](#292)    if let Ok(acls) = db.list_db_acls().await {
[293](#293)        for a in &acls {
[294](#294)            (a.model.as_str(), a.group.as_str(), a.read, a.write, a.create, a.delete).hash(&mut h);
[295](#295)        }
[296](#296)    }
[297](#297)    if let Ok(rules) = db.list_db_rules().await {
[298](#298)        for r in &rules {
[299](#299)            (r.id, r.model.as_str(), r.groups.as_str(), r.ops.as_str(), r.domain.as_str(), r.active)
[300](#300)                .hash(&mut h);
[301](#301)        }
[302](#302)    }
[303](#303)    h.finish()
[304](#304)}

[432](#432)fn build_data_router(
[433](#433)    models: Vec<ResolvedModel>,
[434](#434)    installed: Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>,
[435](#435)    custom_fields: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, Vec<FieldDef>>>>,

[443](#443)) -> Router {
[444](#444)    if let Err(e) = validate_routes() {
[447](#447)        panic!("kigumi-server: {e}");
[448](#448)    }
[449](#449)    let db = Arc::new(db);
[450](#450)    let (events, _) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel::<Arc<Vec<StoredEvent>>>(64);
[451](#451)    spawn_event_poller(db.clone(), events.clone());
[452](#452)    base_router()
[453](#453)        .route("/auth/login", post(login_handler))
[454](#454)        .route("/auth/refresh", post(refresh_handler))

[465](#465)        .route("/api/:name", get(list_handler).post(create_handler))

[467](#467)            "/api/:name/:id",

[475](#475)        .route("/api/reports/:report", get(ledger_report_handler))

[498](#498)        .route("/api/:name/:id/message", post(post_message_handler))
[499](#499)        .route("/api/:name/:id/activities", get(activities_handler))
[501](#501)        .route("/api/:name/:id/activity", post(schedule_activity_handler))
[502](#502)        .route("/api/:name/:id/activities/:aid/done", post(activity_done_handler))
[503](#503)        .route("/api/:name/:id/followers", get(followers_handler))
[505](#505)        .route("/api/:name/:id/follow", post(follow_handler))
[506](#506)        .route("/api/:name/:id/unfollow", post(unfollow_handler))
[507](#507)        .with_state(AppState {
[508](#508)            models: Arc::new(models),
[509](#509)            installed,
[510](#510)            custom_fields,
[511](#511)            view_overrides,
[512](#512)            data: Some(DataBackend {
[513](#513)                db,
[514](#514)                events,
[515](#515)                acls,
[516](#516)                rules,
[517](#517)                auth: Arc::new(Authenticator::new(auth_secret)),
[518](#518)                blobs,
[519](#519)                rasterizer,
[520](#520)            }),
[521](#521)        })
[522](#522)        .layer(axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit::max(MAX_BODY_BYTES))
[523](#523)}

[541](#541)
[542](#542)fn spawn_event_poller(db: Arc<Db>, tx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<Arc<Vec<StoredEvent>>>) {
[543](#543)    const TICK_MS: u64 = 250;
[544](#544)    tokio::spawn(async move {
[545](#545)        let mut cursor: Option<(i64, i64)> = None;
[546](#546)        loop {
[547](#547)            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(TICK_MS)).await;
[548](#548)            if tx.receiver_count() == 0 {
[549](#549)                match db.latest_event_cursor().await {
[550](#550)                    Ok(c) => cursor = Some(c),
[551](#551)                    Err(e) => eprintln!("kigumi-server event poller (idle cursor) failed: {e:?}"),
[552](#552)                }
[553](#553)                continue;
[554](#554)            }
[555](#555)            let from = match cursor {
[556](#556)                Some(c) => c,
[557](#557)                None => match db.latest_event_cursor().await {
[558](#558)                    Ok(c) => c,
[559](#559)                    Err(e) => {
[560](#560)                        eprintln!("kigumi-server event poller (cursor) failed: {e:?}");
[561](#561)                        continue;
[562](#562)                    }
[563](#563)                },
[564](#564)            };
[565](#565)            match db.events_after(from, 200).await {
[566](#566)                Ok(events) if events.is_empty() => {
[567](#567)                    cursor = Some(from);
[568](#568)                }
[569](#569)                Ok(events) => {
[570](#570)                    cursor = Some(events.last().map(|e| (e.txn, e.id)).unwrap_or(from));
[571](#571)                    let _ = tx.send(Arc::new(events)); }
[573](#573)                Err(e) => eprintln!("kigumi-server event poller failed: {e:?}"),
[574](#574)            }
[575](#575)        }
[576](#576)    });
[577](#577)}

[579](#579)fn authenticate(backend: &DataBackend, headers: &HeaderMap) -> Result<Ctx, Response> {
[582](#582)    let header = headers.get("authorization").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());
[583](#583)    backend
[584](#584)        .auth
[585](#585)        .verify_bearer(header)
[586](#586)        .map_err(|_| (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "unauthorized").into_response())

[597](#597)fn resolve_model(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> Result<ResolvedModel, Response> {
[602](#602)    let base = state
[603](#603)        .models
[604](#604)        .iter()
[605](#605)        .find(|m| m.name == name)
[606](#606)        .filter(|_| is_served(state, name))
[607](#607)        .ok_or_else(|| (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("unknown model: {name}")).into_response())?;
[608](#608)    let mut model = base.clone();
[609](#609)    if let Ok(map) = state.custom_fields.read() {
[610](#610)        if let Some(extra) = map.get(name) {
[611](#611)            model.fields.extend(extra.iter().copied());
[612](#612)        }
[613](#613)    }
[614](#614)    Ok(model)

[617](#617)fn error_response(status: StatusCode, code: &str, message: &str, fields: &[(String, String)]) -> Response {
[622](#622)    let mut err = serde_json::Map::new();
[623](#623)    err.insert("code".into(), serde_json::Value::String(code.to_string()));
[624](#624)    err.insert("message".into(), serde_json::Value::String(message.to_string()));
[625](#625)    if !fields.is_empty() {
[626](#626)        let mut map = serde_json::Map::new();
[627](#627)        for (field, msg) in fields {
[628](#628)            map.entry(field.clone())
[629](#629)                .or_insert_with(|| serde_json::Value::Array(Vec::new()))
[630](#630)                .as_array_mut()
[631](#631)                .expect("fields entries are arrays")
[632](#632)                .push(serde_json::Value::String(msg.clone()));
[633](#633)        }
[634](#634)        err.insert("fields".into(), serde_json::Value::Object(map));
[635](#635)    }
[636](#636)    let body = serde_json::json!({ "error": err }).to_string();
[637](#637)    (status, [("content-type", "application/json")], body).into_response()
[638](#638)}
[639](#639)
[640](#640)fn write_error(context: &str, e: DbError) -> Response {
[642](#642)    match e {
[643](#643)        DbError::AccessDenied { .. } => error_response(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "access-denied", "access denied", &[]),
[644](#644)        DbError::BadInput(msg) => error_response(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "bad-input", &msg, &[]),
[645](#645)        DbError::Invalid { message, fields } => error_response(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "invalid", &message, &fields),
[646](#646)        DbError::Conflict(msg) => error_response(StatusCode::CONFLICT, "conflict", &msg, &[]),
[647](#647)        other => internal_error(context, other),
[648](#648)    }

[704](#704)async fn modules_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
[706](#706)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[707](#707)    if let Err(r) = authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[708](#708)        return r;
[709](#709)    }
[710](#710)    let mods = match resolve_modules() {
[711](#711)        Ok(m) => m,
[712](#712)        Err(e) => return internal_error("modules", e),
[713](#713)    };
[714](#714)    let installed = match backend.db.installed_modules().await {
[715](#715)        Ok(i) => i,
[716](#716)        Err(e) => return write_error("modules", e),
[717](#717)    };
[718](#718)    let items: Vec<serde_json::Value> = mods
[719](#719)        .iter()
[720](#720)        .map(|m| {
[721](#721)            serde_json::json!({
[722](#722)                "name": m.name,
[723](#723)                "version": m.version,
[724](#724)                "summary": m.summary,
[725](#725)                "framework": m.framework,
[726](#726)                "depends": m.depends.iter().map(|d| serde_json::json!({ "name": d.name, "req": d.req })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[727](#727)                "installed": installed.iter().any(|i| i == m.name),
[728](#728)            })
[729](#729)        })
[730](#730)        .collect();
[731](#731)    json_response(serde_json::json!(items).to_string())
[732](#732)}

[734](#734)async fn module_install_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
[739](#739)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[740](#740)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[741](#741)        Ok(c) => c,
[742](#742)        Err(r) => return r,
[743](#743)    };
[744](#744)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[745](#745)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "installing a module requires the admin group").into_response();
[746](#746)    }
[747](#747)    let want = match module_closure(&name) {
[748](#748)        Ok(w) => w,
[749](#749)        Err(e) => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, e).into_response(),
[750](#750)    };
[751](#751)    let mods = match resolve_modules() {
[752](#752)        Ok(m) => m,
[753](#753)        Err(e) => return internal_error("modules", e),
[754](#754)    };
[755](#755)    let mut installed_now: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
[756](#756)    for m in mods.iter().filter(|m| want.contains(&m.name)) {
[757](#757)        match backend.db.is_module_installed(m.name).await {
[758](#758)            Ok(true) => {}
[759](#759)            Ok(false) => match backend.db.mark_module_installed(m.name, m.version).await {
[760](#760)                Ok(_) => installed_now.push(m.name),
[761](#761)                Err(e) => return write_error("module_install", e),
[762](#762)            },
[763](#763)            Err(e) => return write_error("module_install", e),
[764](#764)        }
[765](#765)    }
[766](#766)    if let Err(e) = backend.db.migrate_installed_schema().await {
[769](#769)        return write_error("module_install", e);
[770](#770)    }
[771](#771)    refresh_installed(&state.installed, backend).await;
[772](#772)    json_response(serde_json::json!({ "installed": installed_now, "needs_restart": false }).to_string())
[773](#773)}
[774](#774)
[775](#775)async fn refresh_installed(installed: &Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>, backend: &DataBackend) {
[779](#779)    if let Ok(names) = backend.db.installed_modules().await {
[780](#780)        if let Ok(mut w) = installed.write() {
[781](#781)            *w = names.into_iter().collect();
[782](#782)        }
[783](#783)    }
[784](#784)}
[785](#785)
[786](#786)async fn module_uninstall_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
[789](#789)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[790](#790)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[791](#791)        Ok(c) => c,
[792](#792)        Err(r) => return r,
[793](#793)    };
[794](#794)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[795](#795)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "uninstalling a module requires the admin group").into_response();
[796](#796)    }
[797](#797)    if name == "base" {
[798](#798)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "cannot uninstall 'base' (the foundational module)").into_response();
[799](#799)    }
[800](#800)    match backend.db.is_module_installed(&name).await {
[801](#801)        Ok(false) => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("module '{name}' is not installed")).into_response(),
[802](#802)        Ok(true) => {}
[803](#803)        Err(e) => return write_error("module_uninstall", e),
[804](#804)    }
[805](#805)    let mods = match resolve_modules() {
[806](#806)        Ok(m) => m,
[807](#807)        Err(e) => return internal_error("modules", e),
[808](#808)    };
[809](#809)    let installed = match backend.db.installed_modules().await {
[810](#810)        Ok(i) => i,
[811](#811)        Err(e) => return write_error("modules", e),
[812](#812)    };
[813](#813)    let dependents: Vec<&str> = mods
[814](#814)        .iter()
[815](#815)        .filter(|m| installed.iter().any(|i| i == m.name) && m.depends.iter().any(|d| d.name == name))
[816](#816)        .map(|m| m.name)
[817](#817)        .collect();
[818](#818)    if !dependents.is_empty() {
[819](#819)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("uninstall {dependents:?} first — they depend on '{name}'")).into_response();
[820](#820)    }
[821](#821)    match backend.db.mark_module_uninstalled(&name).await {
[822](#822)        Ok(_) => {
[823](#823)            refresh_installed(&state.installed, backend).await;
[824](#824)            json_response(serde_json::json!({ "uninstalled": name, "needs_restart": false }).to_string())
[825](#825)        }
[826](#826)        Err(e) => write_error("module_uninstall", e),
[827](#827)    }
[828](#828)}
[829](#829)
[830](#830)async fn add_field_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(body): Json<Json2>) -> Response {
[834](#834)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[835](#835)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[836](#836)        Ok(c) => c,
[837](#837)        Err(r) => return r,
[838](#838)    };
[839](#839)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[840](#840)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "adding a field requires the admin group").into_response();
[841](#841)    }
[842](#842)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[843](#843)        Ok(m) => m,
[844](#844)        Err(r) => return r,
[845](#845)    };
[846](#846)    let obj = match body_object(&body) {
[847](#847)        Ok(o) => o,
[848](#848)        Err(r) => return r,
[849](#849)    };
[850](#850)    let Some(fname) = str_field(&body, "name") else {
[851](#851)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "'name' is required").into_response();
[852](#852)    };
[853](#853)    let Some(kind_str) = str_field(&body, "kind") else {
[854](#854)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "'kind' is required").into_response();
[855](#855)    };
[856](#856)    let label = str_field(&body, "label").unwrap_or(fname);
[857](#857)    let required = obj.get("required").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);
[858](#858)    let default = str_field(&body, "default");
[859](#859)    let relation = str_field(&body, "relation");
[861](#861)    let col_type = if kind_str == "many2one" {
[862](#862)        let Some(target) = relation else {
[863](#863)            return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "a many2one field needs a 'relation' (the target model)").into_response();
[864](#864)        };
[865](#865)        if resolve_model(&state, target).is_err() {
[866](#866)            return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("unknown target model '{target}'")).into_response();
[867](#867)        }
[868](#868)        pg_column_type(&FieldKind::Many2one { target: "" })
[869](#869)    } else {
[870](#870)        let Some(kind) = parse_custom_kind(kind_str) else {
[871](#871)            return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("unsupported kind '{kind_str}' (text|integer|float|decimal|bool|date|datetime|many2one)")).into_response();
[872](#872)        };
[873](#873)        pg_column_type(&kind)
[874](#874)    };
[875](#875)    if !is_safe_ident(fname) {
[876](#876)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "field name must be lowercase letters, digits and underscore").into_response();
[877](#877)    }
[878](#878)    if model.fields.iter().any(|f| f.name == fname) {
[879](#879)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("field '{fname}' already exists on {name}")).into_response();
[880](#880)    }
[881](#881)    match backend.db.add_custom_field(&name, fname, label, kind_str, required, default, relation, model.table, col_type).await {
[882](#882)        Ok(_) => {
[883](#883)            refresh_custom_fields(&state.custom_fields, &backend.db).await;
[884](#884)            json_response(serde_json::json!({ "added": fname, "model": name }).to_string())
[885](#885)        }
[886](#886)        Err(e) => write_error("add_field", e),
[887](#887)    }
[888](#888)}
[889](#889)
[890](#890)async fn view_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>) -> Response {
[891](#891)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[892](#892)        Ok(m) => m,
[893](#893)        Err(r) => return r,

[895](#895)    let json = match to_ui_contract(&model, &[]) {
[896](#896)        Ok(j) => j,
[897](#897)        Err(e) => return internal_error("view", e),
[898](#898)    };
[899](#899)    let overrides = state

[902](#902)        .read()
[903](#903)        .ok()
[904](#904)        .and_then(|m| m.get(&name).cloned())

[906](#906)    if overrides.is_empty() {

[913](#913)async fn list_view_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>, headers: HeaderMap) -> Response {
[917](#917)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[918](#918)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[919](#919)        Ok(c) => c,
[920](#920)        Err(r) => return r,
[921](#921)    };
[922](#922)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[923](#923)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "viewing overrides requires the admin group").into_response();
[924](#924)    }
[925](#925)    let rows = state
[926](#926)        .view_overrides
[927](#927)        .read()
[928](#928)        .ok()
[929](#929)        .and_then(|m| m.get(&name).cloned())
[930](#930)        .unwrap_or_default();
[931](#931)    let cond = |s: &Option<String>| -> Json2 {
[934](#934)        s.as_deref().and_then(|d| serde_json::from_str::<Json2>(d).ok()).unwrap_or(Json2::Null)
[935](#935)    };
[936](#936)    let items: Vec<Json2> = rows
[937](#937)        .iter()
[938](#938)        .map(|o| {
[939](#939)            serde_json::json!({
[940](#940)                "field": o.field,
[941](#941)                "label": o.label,
[942](#942)                "widget": o.widget,
[943](#943)                "invisible": o.invisible,
[944](#944)                "readonly": o.readonly,
[945](#945)                "invisible_when": cond(&o.invisible_when),
[946](#946)                "readonly_when": cond(&o.readonly_when),
[947](#947)            })
[948](#948)        })
[949](#949)        .collect();
[950](#950)    json_response(serde_json::Value::Array(items).to_string())
[951](#951)}

[953](#953)async fn add_view_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(name): Path<String>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(body): Json<Json2>) -> Response {
[959](#959)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[960](#960)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[961](#961)        Ok(c) => c,
[962](#962)        Err(r) => return r,
[963](#963)    };
[964](#964)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[965](#965)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "overriding a view requires the admin group").into_response();
[966](#966)    }
[967](#967)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[968](#968)        Ok(m) => m,
[969](#969)        Err(r) => return r,
[970](#970)    };
[971](#971)    let Some(field) = str_field(&body, "field") else {
[972](#972)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "'field' is required").into_response();
[973](#973)    };
[974](#974)    let known = model.fields.iter().any(|f| f.name == field)
[977](#977)        || delegated_fields(&name).unwrap_or_default().iter().any(|d| d.def.name == field);
[978](#978)    if !known {
[979](#979)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("unknown field '{field}' on {name}")).into_response();
[980](#980)    }
[981](#981)    let existing = state
[985](#985)        .view_overrides
[986](#986)        .read()
[987](#987)        .ok()
[988](#988)        .and_then(|m| m.get(&name).and_then(|v| v.iter().find(|o| o.field == field).cloned()));
[989](#989)    let label = if body.get("label").is_some() {
[990](#990)        str_field(&body, "label").map(str::to_string)
[991](#991)    } else {
[992](#992)        existing.as_ref().and_then(|e| e.label.clone())
[993](#993)    };
[994](#994)    let widget = if body.get("widget").is_some() {
[995](#995)        str_field(&body, "widget").map(str::to_string)
[996](#996)    } else {
[997](#997)        existing.as_ref().and_then(|e| e.widget.clone())
[998](#998)    };
[999](#999)    let bool_field = |k: &str, prev: bool| match body.get(k) {
[1000](#1000)        Some(v) => v.as_bool().unwrap_or(false),
[1001](#1001)        None => prev,
[1002](#1002)    };
[1003](#1003)    let invisible = bool_field("invisible", existing.as_ref().map(|e| e.invisible).unwrap_or(false));
[1004](#1004)    let readonly = bool_field("readonly", existing.as_ref().map(|e| e.readonly).unwrap_or(false));
[1005](#1005)    let parse_cond = |key: &str, prev: Option<String>| -> Result<Option<String>, Response> {
[1008](#1008)        if body.get(key).is_none() {
[1009](#1009)            return Ok(prev);
[1010](#1010)        }
[1011](#1011)        match body.get(key).filter(|v| !v.is_null()) {
[1012](#1012)            None => Ok(None),
[1013](#1013)            Some(d) => {
[1014](#1014)                let json = d.to_string();
[1015](#1015)                Domain::from_json(&json)
[1016](#1016)                    .and_then(|dm| dm.validate(&model))
[1017](#1017)                    .map_err(|e| (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("invalid {key}: {e:?}")).into_response())?;
[1018](#1018)                Ok(Some(json))
[1019](#1019)            }
[1020](#1020)        }
[1021](#1021)    };
[1022](#1022)    let invisible_when = match parse_cond("invisible_when", existing.as_ref().and_then(|e| e.invisible_when.clone())) {
[1023](#1023)        Ok(v) => v,
[1024](#1024)        Err(r) => return r,
[1025](#1025)    };
[1026](#1026)    let readonly_when = match parse_cond("readonly_when", existing.as_ref().and_then(|e| e.readonly_when.clone())) {
[1027](#1027)        Ok(v) => v,
[1028](#1028)        Err(r) => return r,
[1029](#1029)    };
[1030](#1030)    match backend
[1031](#1031)        .db
[1032](#1032)        .set_view_override(
[1033](#1033)            &name,
[1034](#1034)            field,
[1035](#1035)            label.as_deref(),
[1036](#1036)            widget.as_deref(),
[1037](#1037)            invisible,
[1038](#1038)            readonly,
[1039](#1039)            invisible_when.as_deref(),
[1040](#1040)            readonly_when.as_deref(),
[1041](#1041)        )
[1042](#1042)        .await
[1043](#1043)    {
[1044](#1044)        Ok(_) => {
[1045](#1045)            refresh_view_overrides(&state.view_overrides, &backend.db).await;
[1046](#1046)            json_response(serde_json::json!({ "view": { "model": name, "field": field } }).to_string())
[1047](#1047)        }
[1048](#1048)        Err(e) => write_error("set_view", e),
[1049](#1049)    }
[1050](#1050)}

[1150](#1150)async fn set_rule_handler(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(body): Json<Json2>) -> Response {
[1158](#1158)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1159](#1159)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1160](#1160)        Ok(c) => c,
[1161](#1161)        Err(r) => return r,
[1162](#1162)    };
[1163](#1163)    if !ctx.is_member("admin") {
[1164](#1164)        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "managing access requires the admin group").into_response();
[1165](#1165)    }
[1166](#1166)    let Some(model) = str_field(&body, "model") else {
[1167](#1167)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "'model' is required").into_response();

[1169](#1169)    let Some(domain) = body.get("domain").filter(|v| !v.is_null()) else {

[1171](#1171)    };
[1172](#1172)    let domain_json = domain.to_string();

[1194](#1194)const DEFAULT_LIMIT: i64 = 80;
[1195](#1195)const MAX_LIMIT: i64 = 500;
[1196](#1196)
[1197](#1197)async fn list_handler(
[1198](#1198)    State(state): State<AppState>,
[1199](#1199)    Path(name): Path<String>,
[1200](#1200)    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
[1201](#1201)    headers: HeaderMap,
[1202](#1202)) -> Response {
[1203](#1203)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[1204](#1204)        Ok(m) => m,
[1205](#1205)        Err(r) => return r,
[1206](#1206)    };
[1207](#1207)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1208](#1208)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1209](#1209)        Ok(c) => c,
[1210](#1210)        Err(r) => return r,
[1211](#1211)    };
[1212](#1212)    let (filter, order, limit, offset) = match parse_list_query(&model, ¶ms) {
[1213](#1213)        Ok(p) => p,
[1214](#1214)        Err(r) => return r,
[1215](#1215)    };
[1216](#1216)    match backend
[1217](#1217)        .db
[1218](#1218)        .list_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), filter.as_ref(), &order, limit, offset)
[1219](#1219)        .await
[1220](#1220)    {
[1221](#1221)        Ok(page) => {
[1222](#1222)            let body = serde_json::json!({
[1223](#1223)                "data": page.data, "total": page.total, "limit": limit, "offset": offset,
[1224](#1224)            });
[1225](#1225)            json_response(body.to_string())
[1226](#1226)        }
[1227](#1227)        Err(DbError::AccessDenied { .. }) => (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "access denied").into_response(),
[1228](#1228)        Err(DbError::BadInput(msg)) => bad_request(msg),
[1229](#1229)        Err(DbError::Domain(e)) => bad_request(format!("invalid filter: {e:?}")),
[1230](#1230)        Err(e) => internal_error("data", e),
[1231](#1231)    }
[1232](#1232)}
[1233](#1233)
[1234](#1234)fn bad_request(msg: String) -> Response {
[1235](#1235)    (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, msg).into_response()
[1236](#1236)}
[1237](#1237)
[1238](#1238)fn parse_list_query(
[1242](#1242)    model: &ResolvedModel,
[1243](#1243)    params: &HashMap<String, String>,
[1244](#1244)) -> Result<(Option<Domain>, Vec<(String, bool)>, i64, i64), Response> {
[1245](#1245)    let mut conds: Vec<Domain> = Vec::new();
[1246](#1246)    if let Some(js) = params.get("domain") {
[1247](#1247)        match Domain::from_json(js) {
[1248](#1248)            Ok(d) => conds.push(d),
[1249](#1249)            Err(e) => return Err(bad_request(format!("invalid domain JSON: {e:?}"))),
[1250](#1250)        }
[1251](#1251)    }
[1252](#1252)    for (key, raw) in params {
[1253](#1253)        if matches!(key.as_str(), "domain" | "order" | "limit" | "offset") {
[1254](#1254)            continue;
[1255](#1255)        }
[1256](#1256)        let (field, op) = split_suffix(key);
[1257](#1257)        conds.push(build_leaf(model, field, op, raw).map_err(bad_request)?);
[1258](#1258)    }
[1259](#1259)    let filter = conds.into_iter().reduce(|a, b| a.and(b));
[1260](#1260)
[1261](#1261)    let mut order = Vec::new();
[1262](#1262)    if let Some(o) = params.get("order") {
[1263](#1263)        for part in o.split(',').map(|s| s.trim()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
[1264](#1264)            match part.strip_prefix('-') {
[1265](#1265)                Some(f) => order.push((f.to_string(), true)),
[1266](#1266)                None => order.push((part.to_string(), false)),
[1267](#1267)            }
[1268](#1268)        }
[1269](#1269)    }
[1270](#1270)
[1271](#1271)    let limit = match params.get("limit") {
[1272](#1272)        Some(s) => s.parse::<i64>().map_err(|_| bad_request("limit must be an integer".into()))?.clamp(1, MAX_LIMIT),
[1273](#1273)        None => DEFAULT_LIMIT,
[1274](#1274)    };
[1275](#1275)    let offset = match params.get("offset") {
[1276](#1276)        Some(s) => s.parse::<i64>().map_err(|_| bad_request("offset must be an integer".into()))?.max(0),
[1277](#1277)        None => 0,
[1278](#1278)    };
[1279](#1279)    Ok((filter, order, limit, offset))
[1280](#1280)}
[1281](#1281)
[1282](#1282)fn split_suffix(key: &str) -> (&str, &str) {
[1284](#1284)    match key.rfind("__") {
[1285](#1285)        Some(i) => (&key[..i], &key[i + 2..]),
[1286](#1286)        None => (key, "eq"),
[1287](#1287)    }
[1288](#1288)}
[1289](#1289)
[1290](#1290)fn build_leaf(model: &ResolvedModel, field: &str, op: &str, raw: &str) -> Result<Domain, String> {
[1292](#1292)    let kind = if field == "id" {
[1293](#1293)        FieldKind::Integer
[1294](#1294)    } else {
[1295](#1295)        model
[1296](#1296)            .fields
[1297](#1297)            .iter()
[1298](#1298)            .find(|f| f.name == field)
[1299](#1299)            .map(|f| f.kind)
[1300](#1300)            .ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown filter field '{field}'"))?
[1301](#1301)    };
[1302](#1302)    let operator = match op {
[1303](#1303)        "eq" => Operator::Eq,
[1304](#1304)        "ne" => Operator::Ne,
[1305](#1305)        "gt" => Operator::Gt,
[1306](#1306)        "gte" => Operator::Ge,
[1307](#1307)        "lt" => Operator::Lt,
[1308](#1308)        "lte" => Operator::Le,
[1309](#1309)        "like" => Operator::Like,
[1310](#1310)        "ilike" => Operator::ILike,
[1311](#1311)        "in" => Operator::In,
[1312](#1312)        other => return Err(format!("unknown operator suffix '__{other}'")),
[1313](#1313)    };
[1314](#1314)    let value = if operator == Operator::In {
[1315](#1315)        Value::List(raw.split(',').map(|s| coerce(&kind, s.trim())).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?)
[1316](#1316)    } else {
[1317](#1317)        coerce(&kind, raw)?
[1318](#1318)    };
[1319](#1319)    Ok(Domain::Cond(Condition { field: field.to_string(), op: operator, value }))
[1320](#1320)}
[1321](#1321)
[1322](#1322)fn coerce(kind: &FieldKind, raw: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
[1324](#1324)    Ok(match kind {
[1325](#1325)        FieldKind::Integer | FieldKind::Many2one { .. } | FieldKind::Image => {
[1326](#1326)            Value::Int(raw.parse().map_err(|_| format!("'{raw}' is not an integer"))?)
[1327](#1327)        }
[1328](#1328)        FieldKind::Decimal { .. } => {
[1329](#1329)            Value::Decimal(raw.parse::<rust_decimal::Decimal>().map_err(|_| format!("'{raw}' is not a number"))?)
[1330](#1330)        }
[1331](#1331)        FieldKind::Float => Value::Float(raw.parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| format!("'{raw}' is not a number"))?),
[1332](#1332)        FieldKind::Bool => Value::Bool(matches!(raw, "true" | "1" | "t" | "yes")),
[1333](#1333)        FieldKind::Text | FieldKind::Html | FieldKind::Selection(_) | FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime => {
[1335](#1335)            Value::Str(raw.to_string())
[1336](#1336)        }
[1337](#1337)        FieldKind::One2many { .. } | FieldKind::Many2many { .. } => {
[1338](#1338)            return Err("cannot filter on a One2many/Many2many field directly".to_string())
[1339](#1339)        }
[1340](#1340)    })
[1341](#1341)}

[1357](#1357)    match backend.db.find_one_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), id).await {

[1369](#1369)        .ok_or_else(|| (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "body must be a JSON object").into_response())

[1397](#1397)async fn update_handler(
[1398](#1398)    State(state): State<AppState>,
[1399](#1399)    Path((name, id)): Path<(String, i64)>,
[1400](#1400)    headers: HeaderMap,

[1404](#1404)        Ok(m) => m,
[1405](#1405)        Err(r) => return r,
[1406](#1406)    };
[1407](#1407)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1408](#1408)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1409](#1409)        Ok(c) => c,
[1410](#1410)        Err(r) => return r,
[1411](#1411)    };
[1412](#1412)    let obj = match body_object(&body) {
[1413](#1413)        Ok(o) => o,
[1414](#1414)        Err(r) => return r,
[1415](#1415)    };
[1416](#1416)    match backend.db.update_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), id, obj).await {
[1417](#1417)        Ok(0) => (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "not found or not permitted").into_response(),
[1418](#1418)        Ok(n) => json_status(StatusCode::OK, format!("{{\"updated\": {n}}}")),
[1419](#1419)        Err(e) => write_error("update", e),
[1420](#1420)    }

[1472](#1472)async fn events_stream_handler(
[1482](#1482)    State(state): State<AppState>,
[1483](#1483)    Query(params): Query<HashMap<String, String>>,
[1484](#1484)    headers: HeaderMap,
[1485](#1485)) -> Response {
[1486](#1486)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1487](#1487)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1488](#1488)        Ok(c) => c,
[1489](#1489)        Err(r) => return r,
[1490](#1490)    };
[1491](#1491)    let models: Vec<String> = params
[1492](#1492)        .get("models")
[1493](#1493)        .map(|m| m.split(',').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(str::to_string).collect())
[1494](#1494)        .unwrap_or_default();
[1495](#1495)    let resume: Option<(i64, i64)> = headers.get("last-event-id").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()).and_then(|v| {
[1498](#1498)        match v.split_once(':') {
[1499](#1499)            Some((t, i)) => Some((t.parse().ok()?, i.parse().ok()?)),
[1500](#1500)            None => Some((0, v.parse().ok()?)),
[1501](#1501)        }
[1502](#1502)    });
[1503](#1503)    let mut rx = backend.events.subscribe();
[1504](#1504)    let db = backend.db.clone();
[1505](#1505)    let acl_state = backend.acls.clone();
[1506](#1506)    let rule_state = backend.rules.clone();
[1507](#1507)
[1508](#1508)    let stream = async_stream::stream! {
[1509](#1509)        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(ACCESS_TTL);
[1510](#1510)        let mut last: (i64, i64) = match resume {
[1511](#1511)            Some(c) => c,
[1512](#1512)            None => match db.latest_event_cursor().await {
[1513](#1513)                Ok(c) => c,
[1514](#1514)                Err(e) => {
[1515](#1515)                    eprintln!("kigumi-server event stream (cursor) failed: {e:?}");
[1516](#1516)                    return;
[1517](#1517)                }
[1518](#1518)            },
[1519](#1519)        };
[1520](#1520)        let wanted = |ev: &StoredEvent| models.is_empty() || models.iter().any(|m| *m == ev.model);
[1521](#1521)        loop {
[1524](#1524)            loop {
[1526](#1526)                let page = match db.events_after(last, 200).await {
[1527](#1527)                    Ok(p) => p,
[1528](#1528)                    Err(e) => {
[1529](#1529)                        eprintln!("kigumi-server event stream (catch-up) failed: {e:?}");
[1530](#1530)                        return;
[1531](#1531)                    }
[1532](#1532)                };
[1533](#1533)                if page.is_empty() {
[1534](#1534)                    break;
[1535](#1535)                }
[1536](#1536)                last = page.last().map(|e| (e.txn, e.id)).unwrap_or(last);
[1537](#1537)                let mine: Vec<StoredEvent> = page.into_iter().filter(|e| wanted(e)).collect();
[1538](#1538)                if mine.is_empty() {
[1539](#1539)                    continue;
[1540](#1540)                }
[1541](#1541)                let (acls, rules) = (snapshot(&acl_state), snapshot(&rule_state));
[1543](#1543)                match db.visible_events(&ctx, &acls, &rules, &mine).await {
[1544](#1544)                    Ok(shaped) => {
[1545](#1545)                        for ev in shaped {
[1546](#1546)                            yield Ok::<_, std::convert::Infallible>(
[1547](#1547)                                axum::response::sse::Event::default().id(sse_id(&ev)).data(ev.to_string()),
[1548](#1548)                            );
[1549](#1549)                        }
[1550](#1550)                    }
[1551](#1551)                    Err(e) => eprintln!("kigumi-server event stream (filter) failed: {e:?}"),
[1553](#1553)                }
[1554](#1554)            }
[1555](#1555)            let remaining = deadline.saturating_duration_since(tokio::time::Instant::now());
[1557](#1557)            if remaining.is_zero() {
[1558](#1558)                return;
[1559](#1559)            }
[1560](#1560)            match tokio::time::timeout(remaining, rx.recv()).await {
[1561](#1561)                Err(_) => return, Ok(Ok(batch)) => {
[1563](#1563)                    let mine: Vec<StoredEvent> = batch
[1564](#1564)                        .iter()
[1565](#1565)                        .filter(|e| (e.txn, e.id) > last && wanted(e))
[1566](#1566)                        .cloned()
[1567](#1567)                        .collect();
[1568](#1568)                    if let Some(max) = batch.last().map(|e| (e.txn, e.id)) {
[1569](#1569)                        last = last.max(max);
[1570](#1570)                    }
[1571](#1571)                    if mine.is_empty() {
[1572](#1572)                        continue;
[1573](#1573)                    }
[1574](#1574)                    let (acls, rules) = (snapshot(&acl_state), snapshot(&rule_state));
[1575](#1575)                    match db.visible_events(&ctx, &acls, &rules, &mine).await {
[1576](#1576)                        Ok(shaped) => {
[1577](#1577)                            for ev in shaped {
[1578](#1578)                                yield Ok(axum::response::sse::Event::default().id(sse_id(&ev)).data(ev.to_string()));
[1579](#1579)                            }
[1580](#1580)                        }
[1581](#1581)                        Err(e) => eprintln!("kigumi-server event stream (filter) failed: {e:?}"),
[1582](#1582)                    }
[1583](#1583)                }
[1584](#1584)                Ok(Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_))) => continue,
[1586](#1586)                Ok(Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed)) => return,
[1587](#1587)            }
[1588](#1588)        }
[1589](#1589)    };
[1590](#1590)    axum::response::Sse::new(stream)
[1591](#1591)        .keep_alive(axum::response::sse::KeepAlive::new().interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(15)))
[1592](#1592)        .into_response()
[1593](#1593)}
[1594](#1594)
[1595](#1595)async fn module_route_handler(
[1602](#1602)    state: AppState,
[1603](#1603)    method: RouteMethod,
[1604](#1604)    route: String,
[1605](#1605)    headers: HeaderMap,
[1606](#1606)    query: HashMap<String, String>,
[1607](#1607)    raw_body: Bytes,
[1608](#1608)) -> Response {
[1609](#1609)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1610](#1610)    let Some(reg) = route_for(&route, method) else {
[1611](#1611)        let others = route_methods(&route);
[1612](#1612)        if others.is_empty() {
[1613](#1613)            return (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("unknown route: {route}")).into_response();
[1614](#1614)        }
[1615](#1615)        let all_auth = others.iter().all(|m| route_for(&route, *m).map(|r| r.auth).unwrap_or(true));
[1618](#1618)        if all_auth {
[1619](#1619)            if let Err(r) = authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1620](#1620)                return r;
[1621](#1621)            }
[1622](#1622)        }
[1623](#1623)        let allow = others
[1624](#1624)            .iter()
[1625](#1625)            .map(|m| match m {
[1626](#1626)                RouteMethod::Get => "GET",
[1627](#1627)                RouteMethod::Post => "POST",
[1628](#1628)            })
[1629](#1629)            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[1630](#1630)            .join(", ");
[1631](#1631)        return (StatusCode::METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, [("allow", allow)], "method not allowed").into_response();
[1632](#1632)    };
[1633](#1633)    let ctx = if reg.auth {
[1634](#1634)        match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1635](#1635)            Ok(c) => c,
[1636](#1636)            Err(r) => return r,
[1637](#1637)        }
[1638](#1638)    } else {
[1639](#1639)        Ctx::new(-1, vec![])
[1642](#1642)    };
[1643](#1643)    let mut hdrs = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
[1646](#1646)    for (name, value) in headers.iter() {
[1647](#1647)        if let Ok(v) = value.to_str() {
[1648](#1648)            hdrs.entry(name.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase())
[1649](#1649)                .and_modify(|cur: &mut String| {
[1650](#1650)                    cur.push_str(", ");
[1651](#1651)                    cur.push_str(v);
[1652](#1652)                })
[1653](#1653)                .or_insert_with(|| v.to_string());
[1654](#1654)        }
[1655](#1655)    }
[1656](#1656)    let body_map = match serde_json::from_slice::<Json2>(&raw_body) {
[1659](#1659)        Ok(Json2::Object(m)) => m,
[1660](#1660)        _ => serde_json::Map::new(),
[1661](#1661)    };
[1662](#1662)    let input = RouteInput {
[1663](#1663)        ctx,
[1664](#1664)        query: query.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, Json2::String(v))).collect(),
[1665](#1665)        body: body_map,
[1666](#1666)        raw_body: raw_body.to_vec(),
[1667](#1667)        headers: hdrs,
[1668](#1668)    };
[1669](#1669)    match backend.db.run_route(reg, input).await {
[1670](#1670)        Ok(RouteOutput::Json(json)) => (
[1671](#1671)            [("content-type", "application/json"), ("x-content-type-options", "nosniff")],
[1672](#1672)            json.to_string(),
[1673](#1673)        )
[1674](#1674)            .into_response(),
[1675](#1675)        Ok(RouteOutput::Text(text)) => (
[1676](#1676)            StatusCode::OK,
[1677](#1677)            [("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8"), ("x-content-type-options", "nosniff")],
[1678](#1678)            text,
[1679](#1679)        )
[1680](#1680)            .into_response(),
[1681](#1681)        Err(e) => write_error("route", e),
[1682](#1682)    }
[1683](#1683)}
[1684](#1684)

[1728](#1728)fn value_to_json(v: &Value) -> Json2 {
[1731](#1731)    match v {
[1732](#1732)        Value::Str(s) => Json2::String(s.clone()),
[1733](#1733)        Value::Int(n) => Json2::Number((*n).into()),
[1734](#1734)        Value::Float(f) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(*f).map(Json2::Number).unwrap_or(Json2::Null),
[1735](#1735)        Value::Decimal(d) => Json2::String(d.to_string()),
[1736](#1736)        Value::Bool(b) => Json2::Bool(*b),
[1737](#1737)        Value::Null => Json2::Null,
[1738](#1738)        Value::List(xs) => Json2::Array(xs.iter().map(value_to_json).collect()),
[1739](#1739)    }
[1740](#1740)}

[1742](#1742)async fn report_handler(
[1746](#1746)    State(state): State<AppState>,
[1747](#1747)    Path((name, id, report)): Path<(String, i64, String)>,
[1748](#1748)    Query(params): Query<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>>,
[1749](#1749)    headers: HeaderMap,
[1750](#1750)) -> Response {
[1751](#1751)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[1752](#1752)        Ok(m) => m,
[1753](#1753)        Err(r) => return r,
[1754](#1754)    };
[1755](#1755)    let Some(reg) = report_for(&name, &report) else {
[1756](#1756)        return (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "unknown report").into_response();
[1757](#1757)    };
[1758](#1758)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1759](#1759)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1760](#1760)        Ok(c) => c,
[1761](#1761)        Err(r) => return r,
[1762](#1762)    };
[1763](#1763)    let want_pdf = params.get("format").map(|f| f == "pdf").unwrap_or(false);
[1764](#1764)    match backend.db.find_one_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), id).await {
[1765](#1765)        Ok(Some(rec)) => {
[1766](#1766)            let html = (reg.func)(&rec);
[1767](#1767)            if !want_pdf {
[1768](#1768)                return axum::response::Html(html).into_response();
[1769](#1769)            }
[1770](#1770)            match &backend.rasterizer {
[1774](#1774)                None => (StatusCode::NOT_IMPLEMENTED, "PDF rendering is not configured").into_response(),
[1775](#1775)                Some(r) => match r.render_pdf(&html) {
[1776](#1776)                    Ok(bytes) => pdf_response(bytes, reg.title, id),
[1777](#1777)                    Err(e) => (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, format!("PDF render failed: {e}")).into_response(),
[1778](#1778)                },
[1779](#1779)            }
[1780](#1780)        }
[1781](#1781)        Ok(None) => (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "not found or not permitted").into_response(),
[1782](#1782)        Err(DbError::AccessDenied { .. }) => (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "access denied").into_response(),
[1783](#1783)        Err(e) => internal_error("report", e),
[1784](#1784)    }
[1785](#1785)}

[1787](#1787)fn pdf_response(bytes: Vec<u8>, title: &str, id: i64) -> Response {
[1790](#1790)    let safe: String = title.chars().map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() { c } else { '_' }).collect();
[1791](#1791)    (
[1792](#1792)        [
[1793](#1793)            (axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/pdf".to_string()),
[1794](#1794)            (axum::http::header::CONTENT_DISPOSITION, format!("inline; filename=\"{safe}-{id}.pdf\"")),
[1795](#1795)        ],
[1796](#1796)        bytes,
[1797](#1797)    )
[1798](#1798)        .into_response()
[1799](#1799)}

[1801](#1801)async fn open_wizard_handler(
[1805](#1805)    State(state): State<AppState>,
[1806](#1806)    Path(name): Path<String>,
[1807](#1807)    headers: HeaderMap,
[1808](#1808)    Json(body): Json<Json2>,
[1809](#1809)) -> Response {
[1810](#1810)    let model = match resolve_model(&state, &name) {
[1811](#1811)        Ok(m) => m,
[1812](#1812)        Err(r) => return r,
[1813](#1813)    };
[1814](#1814)    let Some(wizard) = wizard_for(&name) else {
[1815](#1815)        return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "not a wizard model").into_response();
[1816](#1816)    };
[1817](#1817)    let backend = state.data.as_ref().expect("data backend present on data routes");
[1818](#1818)    let ctx = match authenticate(backend, &headers) {
[1819](#1819)        Ok(c) => c,
[1820](#1820)        Err(r) => return r,
[1821](#1821)    };
[1822](#1822)    let wctx = WizardContext {
[1824](#1824)        active_model: body.get("active_model").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(str::to_string),
[1825](#1825)        active_id: body.get("active_id").and_then(Json2::as_i64),
[1826](#1826)        active_ids: body
[1827](#1827)            .get("active_ids")
[1828](#1828)            .and_then(Json2::as_array)
[1829](#1829)            .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(Json2::as_i64).collect())
[1830](#1830)            .unwrap_or_default(),
[1831](#1831)    };
[1832](#1832)    let seed: serde_json::Map<String, Json2> = (wizard.default_get)(&wctx)
[1833](#1833)        .into_iter()
[1834](#1834)        .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), value_to_json(&v)))
[1835](#1835)        .collect();
[1836](#1836)    let id = match backend.db.insert_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), &seed).await {
[1837](#1837)        Ok(id) => id,
[1838](#1838)        Err(e) => return write_error("open", e),
[1839](#1839)    };
[1840](#1840)    match backend.db.find_one_secured(&model, &ctx, &backend.acls(), &backend.rules(), id).await {
[1841](#1841)        Ok(Some(rec)) => {
[1842](#1842)            json_status(StatusCode::CREATED, serde_json::to_string(&rec).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()))
[1843](#1843)        }
[1844](#1844)        Ok(None) => (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "not found or not permitted").into_response(),
[1845](#1845)        Err(e) => write_error("open", e),
[1846](#1846)    }
[1847](#1847)}

[1895](#1895)fn served_model<'a>(state: &'a AppState, name: &str) -> Result<&'a ResolvedModel, Response> {

[1905](#1905)async fn chatter_setup<'a>(
[1910](#1910)    state: &'a AppState,
[1911](#1911)    headers: &HeaderMap,
[1912](#1912)    name: &str,
[1913](#1913)    id: i64,
